lawyer:
Mosiul Alam, Advocate------  For the Appellants 
Dr M Zahir with Fazlul Karim Chowdhury------  For the Respondent Nos. 1-4
parties:
Ashek Ali (Md) and others  ------ Appellants
Vs.
Abdul Gaffar & others   ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Nozrul Islam Chowdhury J: This appeal at the instance of the defendants as appellants, is directed against the judgment and decree dated 30-7-2000 passed in Title Suit No. 133 of 1993 re-numbered as Title Suit No. 73 of 1997, by the learned Subordinate Judge, now Joint District Judge, Arbitration Court, Dhaka decreeing the suit for Specific Performance of Contract.

2. Facts, in a nutshell, giving rise to this appeal are that one Nazar Ali the predecessor of the defendant Nos. 1-12, was allotted two rehabilitation Plots bearing No. C-338 and C-339 covering a area of 7(seven) kathas within Khilgoan mouza appertaining to CS Plot Nos. 557 and 559 within the city of Dhaka and after such allotment the delivery of possession of the said land was made over in favour of Nazar Ali on 20-11-74, thereafter on 29-9- 81 Nazar Ali entered into an agreement for sale in favour of Jahanara Begum in respect of 2 1/2 katha of land appertaining to western part of plot No. C- 339 at a consideration of Taka 3 (three) lakh upon receipt of an earnest money of Taka 2,99,000 followed by delivery of possession and at that occasion Nazar Ali also executed a power of attorney in favour of Abdul Gaffar the husband of said Jahanara Begum, thereafter on 30-3-82 Nazar Ali also entered into an agreement for sale in favour of Jahanara Begum in respect of the remaining part of plot No. C-339 along with half katha of land appertaining to plot No. 338 i.e. 11/2 katha land (by 2nd bainapatra) at a consideration of Taka 1,71,000 upon receipt of an earnest money amounting to Taka 1 (one) lakh. In the process aforesaid Nazar Ali entered into an agreement for sale of 4 kathas of land in favour of Jahanara Begum at a stage when no registered lease deed was executed in favour of Nazar Ali by the Ministry of Works and the agreement for sale was made only after obtaining letter of allotment from the authority concerned; Nazar Ali during his life time could not execute and register the deed of transfer in favour of Jahanara in view of absence of any registered lease deed in his favour from the Ministry of Works; Nazar Ali died on 8-6-83 leaving behind defendant Nos. 1-12 as his legal heirs, thereafter Jahanara Begum failed to obtain the registered deed of transfer from the heirs of Nazar Ali in respect of the aforesaid 4 (four) kathas of land, therefore, suit for Special Performance of Contract was brought by the heirs of Jahanara Begum since she died before institution of the suit being Title Suit No. 133 of 1993 re-numbered as Title Suit No. 73 of 1997. It is also the case of the plaintiff that the defendant Nos. 8-10 had obtained a registered lease deed in their favour from the Ministry of Works in respect of 2 (two) kathas and 8 Chattak of land out of the said 7 (seven) kathas of land allotted in favour of Nazar Ali.

3. In the said suit two sets of written statements were filed on behalf of the defendants of which one was by the defendants 1-7, 11 and 12, while the other set of written statement was filed by the defendant Nos. 8-10 jointly.

4. In the written statement filed by defendant Nos. 1-7, 11 and 12 they admitted the execution of Bainapatra in favour of Jahanara by their predecessor Nazar Ali but they expressed their inability to execute and register the deed of transfer in view of absence of any registered deed of lease either in favour of Nazar Ali or in favour of his legal heirs. The said answering defendants also disclosed that Nazar Ali had four wives and children out of them; therefore, they were not in a position to join together for the purpose of execution of any deed in favour of Jahanara and or her heirs the plaintiffs in the present suit.

5. The defendant Nos. 8-10, on the other hand, filed their written statement denying the material allegations made in the plaint contending inter alia that Nazar Ali during his life time could not obtain any registered lease deed in his favour in respect of his allotted 7 (seven) kathas of land and after his death the defendant Nos. 1-12 were left behind as his heirs, in the said written statement they also disclosed various sorts of disputes in between the different groups of children out of his four wives they also disclosed in the written statement that they were not aware of the alleged Bainapatra in favour of Jahanara by their predecessor Nazar Ali when the authority concerned found the defendants Nos. 8-10 in possession of 2 and 1/2 kathas of land out of the allot- ted land of Nazar Ali the said 2 and 1/2 kathas was transferred in favour of the said defendant Nos. 8-10 by a registered lease deed executed by the Ministry of Works out of which they are in possession of 1.85 kathas of land and for obtaining possession of the remaining part of their allotted land they have already applied before the proper authority but the authority was not in a position to make over possession of the remaining part of the land leased out in their favour owing to an order of injunction granted by the Court, therefore, defendant Nos. 8-10 prayed for dismissal of the suit.

6. Eventually, the suit was taken up for hearing by the learned Joint District Judge, where plain- tiffs examined 5 (five) witnesses and the defendants examined 6(six) witnesses on their behalf and upon conclusion of the trial the learned Joint District Judge by his judgment and decree dated 30-7-2000 decreed the suit directing the defendant Nos. 1-12 to execute and register a deed of transfer in respect of the suit land in favour of the plaintiffs within 60(sixty) days failing which the said deed would be executed through Court. Against the said judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No. 73 of 1997 the defendant Nos. 8-10 as appellants preferred the instant Appear.

7. Mr Md Mosiul Alam, the learned Advocate appearing for the appellants submits at the very outset that admittedly no registered lease deed was executed by the Ministry of Works in favour of Nazar Ali in respect of his 7(seven) kathas of land during his life time and after obtaining letter of allotment he had allegedly executed two bainapatras one on 29-9-81 and the other one on 30-3-82 and the said two bainapatras are dependent on uncertain future event like registration and the instant suit for Specific Performance of Contract has been brought, for the alleged contract which is hit by section 32 of the Contract Act, 1872.

8. Elaborating his submissions the learned Advocate for the appellants disclosed further that Nazar Ali had no saleable interest at the time when he had entered into the said two contracts for sale in favour of Jahanara, therefore, the same is not at all enforceable under the law. It is also submitted by Mr Moshiul Alam that the instant suit is also hit by section 17 of the Specific Relief Act more particularly when admittedly no registered lease deed has yet been granted in favour of the defendant Nos. 1-7 and 11 and 12 though a fractional part of the leased out land has by now been registered in favour of defendant Nos. 8-10 and admittedly the shares of each of the defendants in the suit land have not yet been demarcated or specified as such unspecified shares of the defendant Nos. 8-10 cannot be enforced by a suit for Specific Performance.

9. It is also submitted by Mr Moshiul Alam, the learned Advocate that in view of the absence of any registered lease deed in favour of all the defendants in respect of the suit land from the Ministry of Works they have no saleable interest in the suit land, as such, any direction given by the Court concerned like the impugned decree must be rendered to be in- fructuous one particularly in view of section 6 of Transfer of Property Act.

10. Substantiating his submissions as aforesaid the learned Advocate for the appellants placed reliance in the case of Ghulam Muhd. Shah vs Fateh Muhammad Shah reported in 7 DLR (FC) 70 (76) and the case of Jagdeo Sharma vs Nandan Mahto reported in AIR 1982 (Pat) 32.

11. Dr M Zahir the learned Counsel appearing with Mr Md Fazlul Karim Chowdhury for the respondent Nos. 1-4 submits that the instant suit is in no way hit by section 17 of the Specific Relief Act rather the defendant Nos. 8-10 having had a lease deed in the meantime in respect of 2 and 1 /2 kathas of land out of the suit land from the Ministry of Works the suit can be decreed in part at the least and in substantiating his submission the learned Advocate placed reliance in the case of Nurun Nessa Khatun vs Saleha Rahman reported in 26 DLR 347.

12. The learned Counsel submits further that the contract involved in the instant suit is not at all a contingent one as contemplated under section 32 of the Contract Act.

13. In view of the fact that the Order of allotment necessarily follows a registered lease deed in favour of the allottee, therefore, the allottee had a legitimate expectation in getting the registered lease deed in his favour and could have transferred or entered into a contract for sale as in the instant case with Jahanara by Nazar Ali. In this connection Dr M Zahir placed reliance in the case of Ghulam Muhd Shah vs Fateh Muhammad Shah reported in 7 DLR (FC) 70. The learned Counsel for the respondents has also referred to section 43 of the Transfer of Property Act to substantiate his submissions that transfer by an unauthorized person but subsequently acquired interest in his favour can also enter into a contract for sale as in the instant case which may be enforeed through Court.

14. Elaborating submission the learned Counsel referred to the fact that the defendant Nos. 8-10 had already obtained a registered lease deed in their favour in respect of 2 and 1/2 kathas of land out of the suit land.

15. In answering the submissions made by the learned Advocate for the appellant Dr M Zahir submits that Specific Performance of Contract may be enforced in part as well. In substantiating his submission the learned Counsel referred to the case of Nurun Nesa Khatun vs Saleha Rahman reported in 26 DLR 347.

16. The learned Counsel also submits that the instant agreement is covered by the provision of section 16 of the Specific Relief Act, as such, its enforcement is sustainable in view and the impugned judgment and decree to the extent of shares of defendant Nos. 8-10 do not warrant any interference by this Court.

17. Heard the learned Advocates, perused the material on record including the decisions referred to by both sides wherefrom it transpires that in the instant case the registered bainapatra dated 29-9- 1981 and another unregistered bainapatra dated 30- 3-1982 were executed by Nazar Ali in favour of Jahanara Begum in respect of the suit land at a stage when he had simply got an allotment letter dated 27- 6-1961 and no registered lease deed was executed in his favour by the Ministry of Works and that Nazar Ali during his life time could not obtain any such lease deed in his favour till his death on 8-6-1983 and even after his death his heirs namely the defendant Nos. 1-7 and 11 and 12 did never receive any registered lease deed in respect of the suit land till date although the defendants Nos. 8-10 has, however, been able to obtain a lease deed in their favour in respect of 2 and 1/2 kathas of land out of the suit land since on an enquiry they were found in possession of 1.85 kathas of land and for acquisition of possession of the remaining part of 2 and 1/2 kathas the defendant Nos. 8-10 and are still fighting.

<u>18. In this suit particularly in the Appeal arising out of the same, the question as to the genuineness or otherwise of the bainapatra, has not been raised at all, therefore, the evidence led by the parties in support or against the same need not be gone into, as such, we do not feel it necessary to go for consideration of the evidence on record more particularly when the factual part of the case, is rather found, no longer disputed.</u>

19. Turning to the point of law raised by the parties in this appeal, particularly Section 32 of the Contract Act which renders certain contracts unenforceable, on scrutiny of the facts we find that Nazar Ali entered into two contracts for sale of the suit land in favour of Jahanara at a stage when title of the land was not admittedly transferred in his favour through any registered lease deed, therefore, the contract was in fact subject to registration of the lease deed in his favour by Ministry of Works and such registration was no doubt an uncertain future event which as a matter of fact, did not take place till date so far as Nazar Ali or his other heirs i.e. defendant Nos. 1-7 and 11-12 are concerned, therefore, the contracts so far as those relate to defendant Nos. 1-7 and 11 and 12 are no doubt contingent ones which under section 32 of the Contract Act is not enforceable.

20. Turning to the other part of the contract so far as it relates to defendant Nos. 8-10, it is evident that they have however, in the meantime obtained a registered leased deed in their favour in respect of 2 and 1/2 kathas of land and possession whereof has not yet been obtained by them fully but in that case too, considering a good member of heirs left behind by the Nazar Ali, we are not supposed to embark upon a task of determination of specific shares obtained by those defendant Nos. 8-10 and under such circumstances the submissions made by Dr M Zahir to the effect that the contract in question is enforceable in part is also not sustainable more particularly when it is evident that the same is not a divisible one.

21. We have also noticed that the case relied on by the learned Counsel for the respondents reported in 26 DLR 347 and having gone through the same we find that the principle of law enunciated in that case also do not come in aid of the learned Counsel for the respondents. In view of the position that in that particular case the shares of the plaintiffs and the defendants were specified namely the shares of the plaintiff's in that particular case was 3/4th while the shares of the defendants 1/4th and there was no dispute as to the shares of the plaintiff and the defendants in that particular, case on the other hand, in the instant case there is no specification of the share of defendant Nos. 8-10 in the suit land and under such circumstances it is also evident that section 17 of the Specific Relief Act operators as a bar in proceeding with the instant suit and in this connection we feel it proper to quote section 17 of the Specific Relief Act which reads as under:-

"17. Bar in other cases of specific performance of part of contract-The Court shall not direct the specific performance of a part of a contract except in cases coming under one or other of the three last preceding sections."

22. In the connection it may be mentioned that three last preceding sections of the Specific Relief Act (of section 17) i.e. sections 14,15 and 16 also do not cover the instant suit, since the contracts involved in this suit are indivisible therefore, part performance thereof, as claimed by the respondents, is not permissible because of the general principle that a contract cannot be enforced in part, as contemplated under section 17 of the Specific Relief Act.

23. Turning to the point raised by Dr M Zahir referring to .section 43 of the Transfer of Property Act that contract by unauthorized person subsequently acquires interest in property contracted is a valid contract and enforceable one. In answering this question it is profitable to quote section 43 of the Transfer of Property Act which reads as under:-

43. Where a person fraudulently or erroneously represents that he is authorized to transfer certain immovable property and professes to transfer such property for consideration, such transfer shall, at the option of the transferee, operate on any interest which the transferor may acquire in such property at any time during which the contract of transfer subsists. Nothing in this section impair the right of transfers in good faith for consideration without notice of the existence of the said option."

24. From a perusal of the aforesaid provision of law we find that for the purpose of application of section 43 of the Transfer of Property Act an element of either fraudulent or erroneous representation by the person who entered into a contract, is necessary, while entering into such contract or sale but in the instant case admittedly there is no such element of either fraud or error in the representation is available by the maker of the contract namely Nazar Ali and, in such view of the matter, we find that section 43 of Transfer of Property Act has got no manner of application in the instant suit rather we find substance in the submission made by the learned Advocate for the appellants to the effect that section 6 of the Transfer of Property Act is also a bar in the instant suit since the contract available in the instant suit on the basis whereof decree also passed was entered into by a person who had merely a possibility of obtaining a registered deed from the Ministry of Works and such possibility of obtaining a registered deed in his favour was not at all transferable although it was done in the instant case by Nazar Ali and taking no notice of any of the situations disclosed above, the trial Court decreed the suit without application of its judicial mind.

25. Lastly, in view of the facts and circumstances disclosed above, it is also evident that Specific Performance of contract is an equitable relief and under certain circumstances such equitable relief cannot be granted particularly when it is found that the decree even if granted, would in fact be rendered infructuous as in the instant case. Since the defendant Nos. 1-7, 11 and 12 cannot be directed to register a deed of transfer in favour of the plaintiff in view of absence of any sale able interest in their favour in respect of the suit land in any form and so far as the defendant Nos. 8-10 are concern their shares in the suit land on the death of their predecessor having not been specified or ascertained they can also not be directed to execute and register a sale deed in favour of the plaintiff although in their independent capacity they have by now acquired a registered lease deed in their favour in respect of  2  and 1/2 kathas of land.

26. In view of what has been started in above, we find substance in the appeal; accordingly, the same is allowed without any order as to costs. Consequently, the impugned judgment and decree dated 30-7-2000 passed by the Sub-ordinate Judge, (Arbitration), Dhaka in Title Suit No. 73 of 1997 is hereby set aside.

Send down the lower Court's record at once.

End.

lawyer:
M Azizul Haque, Senior Advocate and Shamshed Banu, Advocate ------ For the Defendant-Appellant 
Md. Abdul Malek with Md. Ziaur Rehman, Advocates  ------ For the Plaintiff-Respondents.
parties:
Sonali Bank Limited ------ Defendant-Appellants
Vs.
Syed Shakhawat Hossain and ors  ------ Plaintiff- Respondents
full_judgment:
Md. Rezaul Hasan J : This Appeal under Order 43 Rule I(r) of the Code of Civil Procedure (the Code) has been preferred by the defendant- appellant against Order No. 10 dated 27-4-2011, passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 31 of 2011 directing the defendants to maintain statusquo for a period 6 (six) months and prohibiting from taking any step in respect of the suit cold storage. 

2. Facts relevant for disposal of this appeal, are that, one Syed Shakhwat Hossain and four thers, who are respondents Nos. 1-5 before this Court, filed a Title Suit No. 31 of 20 11 against Md. Rezaul Karim, Mukta Begum, Md. Khandaker Amirul Islam Tuku and Sharif Masudul Haque as the defendants Nos.I-4 and also impleading the Sonali Bank, its Managing Director and two Deputy General Mangers as defendants numbers 5 to 8. The plain- tiffs case, in brief, is that they have purchased 100% shares from defendants Nos.I-3, held by them in Mis Combined Food and Cold Storage Ltd. (a private company limited by shares), certificate of incorporation number C-32902 (2023)197); that Form-II7 were executed by the said transfers in favour of the plaintiffs and that the defendant No.1 and 2 have sworn affidavit Nos. 85 and 86 on 26-7- 2006 and the defendant No.3 has sworn affidavit Nos. 17 on 7-8-2006 affirming execution of afore- said share transfer forms in favour of the plaintiffs. Accordingly, the plaintiffs have become 100% owners of the shares in the said company as well as of the landed and other properties, including the cold storage and in the machineries owned by the said company. The plaintiffs have also averred that they are in possession of the properties of the said companies and that they have deposited Tk. 111.49 lakh, in the Bank, as down payment to adjust the loan due to the Bank by the said company. Besides, the plain- tiff have also entered into a partnership arrangement with defendant No.4 on condition that the defendant No.4 would furnish Tk. 3,00,000,00 (three crores) only to enable them to make payment of the Bank loan. Thereafter, the defendants have been trying to change the ownership of the plaintiffs thus acquired by them in the said company and that such an attempt was taken on 20-1-2011. In this situation the plaintiff had no alternative but to file this suit to protect their title and possession in the suit property as well as to avoid suffering irreparable loss. 

3. The plaintiffs have, in the premises, prayed for declaration that the plaintiffs are the exclusive and legal owners of M/s. Combined Food & Cold Storage Ltd. as described in the schedule to the plaint as well as they have prayed for some other consequential reliefs stated in the prayer portion, as follows- 

(খ) নিম্নের খ তফসিলে বর্ণিত ৭নং বিবাদীপক্ষ কর্র্তক ১নং বাদীপক্ষের বরাবরে প্রদত্ত বিগত ২৮-০২-২০১০ ইং তারিখের চিঠি, ৪নং বিবাদীপক্ষ কর্তৃক ১নং বাদীপক্ষের বরাবরে প্রদত্ত বিগত ২২-১২-২০১০ ইং চিঠি এবং বিবাদীপক্ষের কর্তৃক ১নং বাদী রবাবরে প্রদত্ত বিগত ২৪-১২-২০১০ ইং তারিখের চিঠিঅবৈধ, বেআইনি, আকার্স্যকর ও বাদীপক্ষের উপর বাধ্যকর নহে মর্মে অপর এক ঘোষণামূলক ডিক্রী দিতে। 
(গ) নিম্নের ক তফসিল নালিশী মের্সাস কম্বাইন্ড ফুড এন্ড কোন্ড ষ্টোরেজ লিমিটেডতে থাকা বাদীপক্ষের দখল স্থিরতরের ডিক্রি দিতে। 
(ঘ) বাদীপক্ষের মালিক দখলীয় নিম্নের ক তফসিল বর্ণিত নালিশী সম্পত্তি মের্সাস কম্বাইন্ড ফুড এন্ড কোল্ড ষ্টোরেজ লিমিটেড হইতে বিবাদীপক্ষগণ যাহাতে জোরপূর্বক ও বেআনীভাবে বাদীপক্ষকে বা তাহার নিয়োজিত কর্মকর্তা কর্মচারীদেরকে উচ্ছেদ করিয়া বেদখল করিতে না পারে বা উক্ত প্রতিষ্ঠানের জন্য ক্ষতিকর কোন কার্যক্রম করিতে না পারে বা বাদীপক্ষের বৈধ ব্যবসা পরিচালনা করিতে বা উহার সংশ্লিষ্ট যাবতীয় কার্যক্রম পরিচালনা করিতে কোন প্রকার বাধা বিঘ্ন সৃষ্টি করিতে না পারে তৎমর্মে বিবাদীগণের বিরুদ্ধে এক চিরস্থায়ী নিষেধাজ্ঞার ডিক্রী দিতে”

4. Alleging similar facts the plaintiffs have also filed a petition under Order XXXIX, rule 1 and 2 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure, with the prayer that the plaintiffs should not be evicted from the suit property of the M/s Combined Food & Cold Storage Ltd. forcefully or illegally etc. At the same time the plaintiffs have also prayed for an interim order to that effect. 

5. The defendant No.7 Sonali Bank, Corporate Branch (although the Sonali Bank itself is and its branch is the same legal entity) submitted a written objection denying all the material allegation and further stating at paragraph No. 28 that- 

২৮। বাদীর মোকদ্দমা সম্পূর্ণ মিথ্যা, বানোয়াট ও ভিত্তিহীন দাবীর ভিত্তিতে দায়েরকৃত বিধায় বাদীর অস্থায়ী নিষেধাজ্ঞার প্রার্থনা মোতাবেক কোন নিষেধাজ্ঞা পাইতে পারে না। প্রকৃত ঘটনা নিম্নরুপ - মের্সাস কম্বাইন্ড ফুড এন্ড ষ্টোরেজ লিমিটেড একটি প্রাইভেট লিমিটেড কোম্পানী যাহার বর্তমান ব্যবস্থাপনা পরিচালক ৩নং বিবাদী খন্দকার আমিনুল ইসলাম টুকু এবং চেয়ারম্যান ১নং বিবাদী মোঃ রেজাউল ইসলাম এবং পরিচালক ২নং বিবাদী মুক্তা বেগম। উক্ত কোম্পানী একটি আধুনিক হিমাগার প্রতিষ্ঠার জন্য ৭নং বিবাদী সোনালী ব্যাংকের আর্থিক সহায়তা চাহিলে ব্যাংক গত ১৩-০৮-১৯৯৭ ইং তারিখে উক্ত কোম্পানীর অনূকূলে ৩,৫৭,৯৮,০০০ টাকা প্রকল্প ঋণ মনজুর করেন। উক্ত ঋণের জামানত স্বরুপ হিমাগারটি প্রকল্প ভূমিসহ মোট ১.৫৭ একর সম্পত্তি ঋণদাতা সোনালী ব্যাংকের অনুকুলে রেজিঃ মর্টগেজ রাখেন। পরবর্তীতে বিভিন্ন সময়ে কোম্পানীর অনুকূলে বিপুল অংকের চলতি মূলধন ঋণ মনজুর করা হয় যাহা কোম্পানী ভোগ করতঃ হিমাগার প্লেজমূলে বন্ধকীকৃত আলু বেআইনি ভাবে বিক্রয় করায় টংগীবাড়ী থানায় গত ২৪-১১-২০০২ ইং তারিখে কোম্পানীর পরিচালকগণের বিরুদ্ধে ফৌজদারী মামলা নং৫/০২ দায়ের করা হয়, যাহা বিচারাধীন আছে। ইহা ছাড়া বিবাদী কোম্পানীর নিকট বকেয়া ঋণের ৮,২১,১৯,৭২০ (আট কোটি একুশ লক্ষ ঊনিশ হাজার সাতশত বিশ) টাকা আদায়ের জন্য সোনালী ব্যাংক বাদী হইয়া ১নং অর্তঋণ আদালত, ঢাকায় অর্থঋণ মোঃ নং ৩১০/২০০৩ দায়ের করে, যাহা গত ২১-০৪-২০০৫ ইং তারিখে ব্যাংকের অনুকূলে রায় ও ডিক্রী হয়। উক্ত ডিক্রিজারীর নিমিত্তে অর্থজারী মোঃ নং-৫৭৪/২০০৫ দাদয়ের করিলে বিজ্ঞ আদালতে বন্ধকী সম্পত্তি পরপর দুইবার নিলামে দিয়াও বিক্রয় করিতে ব্যর্থ হইয়া গত ২৭-০৪-২০০৯ এর ৩৩(৫) ধারায় ভোগ দখল ও বেচাবিক্রির ক্ষমতা যুক্তে বাদী সোনালী ব্যাংকের অনুকূলে এক সনদপত্র ইস্যু করে। উক্ত বন্ধকী সম্পত্তির ভোগ দখলের সনদপত্র মোতাবেক বাদী/ডিক্রীদার সোনালী ব্যাংক বন্ধকী সম্পত্তির ভোগ দখলের ও বেচাবিক্রির মালিক হিসাবে উহা নিলামে বিক্রিয়ের জন্য চেষ্ঠা করিয়া ব্যর্থ হইয়া পুনরায় কোম্পানীসহ ১-৩নং বিবাদীগণের বিরুদ্ধে ২য় জারী মোকদ্দমা নং ৯৯/২০১০ দায়ের করেন। যাহাতে গ্রেয়তারী পরওয়ানা বর্তমনে ইস্যু হইয়া বিচারাধীন আছে। চতুর ১নং বিবাদী তাদের  বিরুদ্ধে বিচারাধীন মোকদ্দমা বিদ্যমান থাকা অবস্থায় সম্পূর্ণ বে-আইনি ভাবে নালিশী হিমাগার প্রতিষ্ঠানটি তাহার দখল/ নিয়ন্ত্রণে থাকার কথা থাকিলেও যোগসাজসে বাদীগনকে বুঝাইয়া দেয় মর্মে বাদীদাবী করিতেছে, যাহা ৭নং বিবাদী ব্যাংকের বিনা অনুমতিতে দখল বাদী বা অন্যকে বুঝাইয়া দেওয়ার কোন এখতিয়ার ১নং বিবাদীর নাই বা ছিল না। বাদী ১নং বিাবদীর সাথে যোগসাজেশে নালিশী হিমাগারটি অবৈধ ভাবে দখলের চেষ্টা করিতেছে।

6. It thus appears from the record that, M/s Combined Food & Cold Storage Ltd. is a private company limited by shares and that the defendant No.3 is the Managing Director of the said company, whereas the defendants No.1 and 2 are the Directors of the said company. The company, thereafter, applied to the Sonali Bank Ltd, on 13.08.1997 for loan of Taka 3,57,98,000, in the form of project loan, to establish a modern cold storage. As security for repayment of the said loan, the loan applicant, i.e. the company represented by its Directors, has offered as collateral security the land of the Cold Storage Ltd, measuring 1.57 acres, by way of executing a registered mortgage deed in favour of the Bank. Thereafter, the Bank has subsequently granted working capital loan from time to time in favour of the said company and the working capital loan duly secured by pledging the potatoes stored in the cold storage, owned and established by the company by utilizing the project loan obtained from the Bank. But, the Directors committed breach of the terms and conditions of the pledge deed by illegally selling the pledged potatoes without knowledge of the Bank and without depositing the sale proceeds of the pledged goods in the Bank to adjust the loan account and for that reason the Bank had to file a Criminal Case No. 05 of 2002, which is still pending. Besides, in order to realize the outstanding loan of Taka 8,21,19,720 (eight crores twenty one lakh nineteen thousand and seven hundred twenty), the Bank had filed, in the first Artha Rin Court, Dhaka, Artha Rin Suit No. 310/2003 in which the Artha Rin Court passed judgment and decree in favour of the Bank, on 21-4-2005. On the basis of the said judgment and decree, thus passed in favour of the Bank by the Artha Rin Court, the Bank has started Artha Rin Execution Case No. 574/2005, against the judgment debtors, who are the defendant Nos. 1-5 in Title Suit No. 31 of 2011 and who were the defendants in aforesaid Artha Rin Suit No. 310 of 2003. In the Artha Rin Execution Case No. 574 of 2005, the learned Court had put the mortgaged property in auction twice, but it could not be sold. Hence, the decree-holder Bank filed" an application under section 33 (5) of Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 for issuance of a certificate as per provisions of section 33(5) of the said Ain. The executing Court accordingly issued a certificate in favour of the decree- holder Bank (Sonali Bank) on 27-4-2009, under section 33(5) of the Ain, that reads as follows:- 

কোন সম্পত্তির” ৪উপ-ধারা (১),(২),(২ক),(২খ),(২গ),(৩) ও (৪) এর বিধান অনুসারে বিক্রয় করা সম্ভব না হইলে উক্ত সম্পত্তি, ডিক্রীকৃত বাদী পরিপূর্ণভাবে পরিশোধ না হওয়া পর্যন্ত, দখল ও ভোগের অধিকারসহ ডিক্রীদারের অনুকূলে ন্যস্ত করা হইবে, এবং ডিক্রীদার উপ ধারা (১),(২),(২ক),(২খ),(২গ),(৩) ও (৪) এর বিধান অনুসারে উক্ত সম্পত্তি বিক্রয় করিয়া অপরিশোধিত ডিক্রীর দাবী আদায় করিতে পারিবে, এবং আদালত ঐ মর্মে একটি সার্টিফিকেট ইস্যু করিবে।”

7. The decree holder Bank, as such, having received a certificate to occupy and enjoy the mort- gaged properties, had tried to sell the mortgaged property through auction, but that also did not fetch any positive result. Hence, the decree holder Bank has filed second Artha Rin Execution Case No. 99 of 2010 against all judgment-debtors including the company. In the second Execution Case, warrant of arrest have been issued and is waiting execution, but knowing fully well about the judgment and the decree of the Artha Rin Adalat and about the pendency of the execution case, the plaintiffs have intentionally suppressed the fact that the suit cold storage was in the possession and control of the decree holder Bank, as per the certificate issued under section 33(5) of the Ain, illegally claimed to have transferred its 100% shares of the debtor-company and also claimed to have taken over the possession of the mortgaged properties that was vested in favour of the Bank by the Artha Rin Adalat, as recorded herein before. 

8. Further case, as stated in the written objection, of the Bank is that- 

	প্রকৃতপক্ষে সোনালী ব্যাংকের অর্থায়নে প্রতিষ্ঠিত হিমাগারটি এবং হিমাগারের বন্ধকী সম্পত্তি বন্ধক গ্রহিতা ব্যাংকের বিনা অনুমতিতে দখল বুঝাইয়া দেওয়ার কোন রকম এখতিয়ার ১নং বিবাদীর নাই। বাদীগণ কম্বাইন্ড ফুড এন্ড কোল্ড ষ্টোরেজ লিমিটেড এর কোন প্রকার পরিচালক ও শেয়ার হোল্ডর নহেন। তাহারা উক্ত কোম্পানীর পরিচালক বা শেয়ার হোল্ডার উহা দেখাইবার মত কোন কাগজ তাদের কাছে নাই বা উক্ত কোম্পানীর তাহারা পরিচালক বা শেয়ার হোল্ডার এই মর্মে কোন কাজগ বা দলিলাদী বিজ্ঞ আদালতে দাখিল করেন নাই। মামলাধীন সম্পত্তি কোনরকম হস্তান্তরের কোনরুপ আইনগত অধিকার ১নং-৩নং বিবাদীগণের নাই। বাদীগণ ১-৩নং বিবাদীগণের সাথে অবৈধ যোগসাজশে একটি রাষ্ট্রায়ত্ত্ব বাণিজ্যিক ব্যাংকের বৈধভাবে অর্জিত বন্ধকী সম্পত্তি হইতে বঞ্চিত করার অসৎ উদ্দেশ্যে নালিশী সম্পত্তিতে বে-আইনীভাবে প্রবেশ করিয়া নিজেকে উক্ত প্রতিষ্ঠানের বৈধ মালিক দাবী করিয়া অত্র মিথ্যা ও বানোয়াট মোকদ্দমাটি দায়ের করিয়াছেন। প্রকৃতপক্ষে নালিশী হিমাগারটি একটিলাভজনক ব্যবসায় প্রতিষ্ঠান যাহা অবৈধভাবে আত্মসাৎ করার উদ্দেশ্যে বাদীরা নিজেও উক্ত প্রতিষ্ঠানের মালিক দাবী করিয়া অত্র মিথ্যা মোকদ্দমা দায়ের করিয়াছেন। অত্র মোকদ্দমাটি দায়েরের কোন কারণ কস্মিনকালেও সৃষ্টি হয় নাই। ইহা ছাড়া অর্থঋণ আদালত আইনের বিধান মোতাবেক ৩৩(৫) ধারা মোতাবেক ভোগ দখলের সনদপ্রাপ্ত হওয়ার পর অর্থঋণ আদালত হইতে সম্পত্তির মালিকানা দাবী করিয়া উক্ত আদালত ব্যতীত অন্য কোন আদালতে উক্ত আইনতঃ ন্যায়ত চলিতে পারে না”।

15. Having perused the impugned order, we find that under the title আলোচনা ও সিদ্ধান্ত’ it has been recorded that the defendant No.1, representing the said company, has establish the suit cold storage with the loan obtained from the defendant No.7 (Sonali Bank Ltd.). The suit cold storage has been mortgaged in favour of the defendant No.7 (the Bank). The cold storage was affected by the devastating flood of 1998, there was no power supply and as a result it had to stop its operation. On 20-5-2007 the defendants No. 1-3 (of Title Suit No. 31 of2001) have adopted a resolution to transfers their 100% shares and accordingly executed share transfer form (Form 117), duly affirmed by swearing three affidavits; that the plaintiffs have submitted form 117, three affidavits, application dated 04-3-2010 for power connection, a copy of trade license, a receipt showing payment of electricity bills, a mutation Khatian and a receipt showing payment of Tk. 25 lakh to the defendant No. 07 in the Court. The trial Court has also recorded that the Bank has filed Artha Rin Suit No. 574 of2005 for the realization of Tk. 3,57,98,000 against the said defendant and, after obtaining the judgment and decree in the Artha Rin Suit No. 310 of 2003, the Bank has filed Execution suit No. 574 of2005 and had tried, twice, to sell the mortgaged property in auction. But, having failed to do so the Bank has again filed second Execution Case No. 99 of 2010 and that the defendants were trying to collusively hand over the suit cold storage. Thereafter, the trial Court have found that there was no reliable documents on record to show that the plaintiff has paid to defendant No.I-3 Tk. 40 lakh to purchase the suit cold storage or that it had made payment of Tk. 1,11,49,000 to the Bank as down payment. It has further record that- 
স্বীকৃত মতে বাদী যেহেতু নাঃ হিমাগারের দখল পরিচালনা করিতেছে এবং মূল্য প্রধান করুক বা না করুক ১-৩ নং বিবাদী হইতে হিমাগারের সাকূল্য শেয়ার প্রাপ্ত হইয়াছেন। এমবস্থায় হিমাগার বন্ধ হইলে বা মালিকানা লইয়া জটিলতা সৃষ্টি হইলে পক্ষগণ ছাড়াও কৃষককুলের অপূরণীয় ক্ষতি হইবে।
 
Stating this reason the learned Joint District Judge Mr. Md. Sharif Hossain has passed the impugned order directing the defendants to maintain status-quo for a period of 6(six) months. Being aggrieved, this miscellaneous appeal has been preferred by the Bank as noted above. 

16. As recorded in the impugned order, the defendants No.I-3 (of Title Suit No. 31 of2011) and judgment debtors in the Artha Rin Suit No. 574 of 2005 had adopted a resolution on 20-5-2007 for transferring their 100% shares in favour of the plain- tiffs and these defendants have executed form 117 in favour of the plaintiffs and have also sworn affidavits in support of the transfer of shares. The trial Court, thereafter, has recorded in the impugned order that the defendant No.7 (Sonali Bank) has filed Artha Rin Suit No. 310 of 2003 in Artha Rin Court and obtained judgment and decree in that suit for realization of Tk, 3,57,98,000. Thereafter, the Bank has filed two execution cases, respectively numbered as 574 of 2005 and 99 of 2010, the latter execution case still pending before the Artha Rin Court. 

17. As such Section 27A of Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 1991 reads as follows: "27 A. Restrictions on the directors of the debtor-Bank-Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, no resignation of any director of a debtor- Bank shall be effective and no director of any such Bank shall be entitled to transfer or sell his shares without the consent of the Board of Directors of the loan giving Bank or financial institution." 

18. Learned Joint District Judge has recorded that before effecting the purported transfer pursuant to a resolution dated 20-5-2007 by the share holders of the debtor company, the company itself was a debtor and a defendant in Artha Rin Suit No. 310 of 2003 and a judgment debtor in Artha Rin Execution Case No. 574 of2005. Hence, the question arises as to the validity of transfer of shares by the said three share holder directors in violation of section 27 A of the Bank Companies Act, 1991. 

19. Now, we find that, before and at the time of adopting the resolution dated 20-5-2007 to transfer 100% shares of the said company by executing form117 by the defendant Nos. 1-3 (the judgment debtors of the said Artha Rin Suit) the said company was a debtor to the Bank and the Bank has already filed Artha Rin Suit No. 310 of2003. As such, as per specific and clear provisions of section 27 A of the Bank Companies Act 1991, which is a special law, no transfer of shares was either permitted in law or effective in the eye of law, without the consent of the Board of Directors of the creditor Bank (the Sonali Bank). In the absence of any materials on record showing that the aforesaid defendants No.1-3 had obtained any consent from the Sonali Bank and that upon such consent the entire share of the said company was transferred to the plaintiff, the plaintiffs have acquired no title, right or interest in the shares of the said company or in the cold storage owned and established by the company or in any of its property. As such, the Court below has totally ignored this specific and special provisions of section 27A of the Bank Companies Act, 1991 and has passed the impugned order on an absurd reason that- 
স্বীকৃত মতে বাদী যেহেতু নালিমী হিমাগারের দখল পরিচালনা করিতেছেন এবং মূল্য প্রদান করুক বা না করুক সে ১-৩নং বিবাদী হইতে হিমাগারের সমুদয় শেয়ার প্রাপ্ত হইয়াছে।”

This findings is not only contrary to the specific provisions of law, it is also contrary to the principles of law that no title or interest in any property can be passed without any consideration (except in the case of gift or inheritance). As such, the impugned order is ex facie illegal and is liable to be set aside. 

20. Besides, it is also a long established principle of law that, an interim order in the nature of status-quo or injunction which comes into conflict with any specific provisions of an statute cannot be passed, but the trial Court has passed the impugned order which is in conflict with the provisions of section 27A of the Bank Companies of the Act, 1991 and also with the section 33(5) and section 20 of Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 and both of them are special statutes. 

21. Even the Court below has overlooked and ignored the specific bar imposed by section 20 of Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 attributing fmality to the order of Artha Rin Adalat. Section 20 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain reads as follows-
ধারা-২০। অর্থঋণ আদালতের আদেশের চুড়ান্ত। এই আইনের বিধান ব্যতিরেকে, কোন আদালত বা কর্তৃপক্ষের নিকট ঋণ আদালতে বিচারাধীন কোন কার্যধারা বা উহার কোন আদেশ, রায় বা ডিক্রীর বিষয়ে কোন প্রশ্ন উথাপন করা যাইবে না, এবংএই আইনের বিধানকে উপক্ষে করিয়া কোন আদালত বা কর্তৃপক্ষ গ্রাহ্য করিবে না”।

22. The trial Court having recorded that, the Bank had obtained judgment and decree from Artha Rin Court, in the Artha Rin Suit No. 310 of 2003. But, it has failed to appreciate that no appeal being preferred against the said judgment and decree of the Artha Rin Adalat, the judgment and decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat has acquired finality and has become conclusive. 

 23. Besides the trial Court have also recorded that the Bank had filed Artha Rin Execution Case No. 574 of2004 for realization of the decreatal dues and failed twice to sell the mortgaged property by holding two auctions (in the execution case) and that the Bank has again filed the second Execution Case No. 99 of 20 1 O. In that execution case the Artha Rin Adalat has issued a certificate in favour of the Bank under section 33(5) of Artha Rin Adalat Ain, but the Court below has failed to appreciate that the order of the Artha Rin Adalat have become final and conclusive as per section 20 of the Ain. 

24. At the same time, the Court below has failed to appreciate that it can not sit as a Court of appeal over the judgment and decree or orders of Artha Rin Adalats, which have been established under an special statute. Hence, the impugned order is not only illegal, but it raises the ability of this particular judge to try a case and about his possessing elementary knowledge of laws that are applicable in most of the civil proceedings. 

25. When, prima facie the entire alleged trans- action itself is contrary to the specific provisions of law, namely section 27 A of the Bank Companies Act, 1991 section 20 and 33(5) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 and section 53D of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, the impugned order cannot sustain. Besides, this kind of order would indulgence and frustrate intent of the legislature enacting special law for recovery of the loan sanctioned by the Banks. Bank relies on the public deposit in allowing credit facilities. 

26. Besides, the trial Court ought to have found that the alleged possession was wholly illegal and that the plaintiffs were trespassers in the suit proper- ties and that possession of a trespasser or of any other person instrumental to the trespassers can not get any protection in the manner as has been given by the Court below, who obviously had no jurisdiction to entertain any such application or the suit. 

27. Section 53D reads as follows, "No immoveable Property under registered mortgage shall be re- mortgaged or sold without the written consent of the mortgagee, and any re-mortgage or sale made other- wise shall be void." Now, having noted in the impugned order that- মিলটি ৭নং বিবাদী বরাবর মর্টগেজ দেওয়া আছে” "how the Court below can proceed upon to pass the impugned order? 

28. The Court below has also failed to consider the balance of convenience and inconvenience in this case, while it has totally ignored the fact that the decree-holder Bank holding a certificate under section 33(5) of the Ain, will suffer irreparable loss, if such an order is passed. It has put the Bank into jeopardy by passing the impugned order and there- by frustrating in Artha Rin Execution process to. be disposed off within a bounded time.
 
29. We have found no written objection tiled by the defendant No.I-3 who are alleged to have executed the share transfer form and the situation also supports the argument of the appellant that these defendant Nos.I-3 are acting in collusion with the plaintiffs. 

30. The decision reported in 8 BLD 1999 (AD) 29 = 40 DLR (AD) 62, Mozher Sowdagar vs M. Zahirul Islam, has no manner of application in this case as because the said decision is regarding a suit filed by a bidder along with prayer for temporary injunction to restrain the defendants (Bangladesh Shipping Corporation and others) from selling the vessel to anybody else. The apex Court, in that case, has held that, a tenderer by making highest offer can not acquire any right to purchase the vessel. That case has no manner of application in the case before as. 

31. We find merit in the Rule as well as in the submissions that the appeal should be allowed with exemplary cost against the respondents. In the result, this appeal is allowed with cost of Tk. 50,000 to be paid within 15(fifteen) days of this order being received in the Court below. The Plaintiff-respondents shall make payment of the cost directly to the concerned branch and shall submit receipt thereof in the Court below. The impugned order No. 1.0 dated 27-4-2010, passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka, in Title Suit No. 31 of2011 is hereby set-aside. Let a copy of this judgment and order be sent to the Secretary, Ministry of Law, Justiceand Parliamentary Affairs, for their evaluation of the judicial functions of the learned Judge Mr. Mohammad Sharif Hossain Hayder and another copy of the judgment be also sent to his controlling officer to see if similar orders were passed in any other cases and to evaluate his overall performance as a judicial officer. Let another copy of the judgment be sent to the learned Registrar, Supreme Court for record. The trial Court is directed to dispose off the suit as expeditiously as possible, preferably within 60 (sixty) working days of receiving the Judgment and Order of this Division. Communicate the orders at once. 

End.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 512 of 2016
lawyer:
A. S. M Khalequzzaman Advocate, instructed by Md Nurul Islam Chowdhury Advocate-on-Record ----- For the Petitioner 
Quamrunnesa Advocate, instructed by Mr Zainul Abedin Advocate-on-Record ----- For Respondent Nos.1, 2 & 4-8 
Respondent Nos.3 and 9-54 ----- Not represented
parties:
Ashek Ahmed ----- Petitioner
Vs.
Samsunnahar and others ----- Respondents
case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 21st of April, 2015 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.4342 of 2010).
full_judgment:
Muhammad Imman Ali J. This civil petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 21.04.2015 passed by a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.4342 of 2010 discharging the Rule.

<u>2. The facts, relevant for disposal of the civil petition for leave to appeal, are that respondent Nos.1-8 herein as plaintiffs filed Other Suit No.169 of 1998 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Chakaria, Cox's Bazar for a declaration that the registered sale deed No.4995 dated 23.11.1988 between the plaintiffs and respondent Nos.2 to 37 is void, illegal and without consideration and also for declaration that the registered sale deed Nos.4217, 4218 and 4219 dated 03.09.2990 are illegal, collusive and not binding upon them.</u>

3. The plaintiffs contended, inter alia, that the suit land originally belonged to one Tamim Golal, who transferred 0.60 satak land in favour of his wife Amir Jan, and two sons, namely Abu Hanifa and Mohammad Hanifa by virtue of registered deed No.1982 dated 23.12.1966. Tamim Golal by another registered deed No.1990 dated 22.09.1996 transferred 0.40 satak land in favour of his 3 sons, namely Mohammad Kalu, Mohammad Hanifa and Abu Hanifa and one Ashek Moula. After his death, his heirs inherited 1.72 sataks of land. The plaintiffs and defendant Nos.2 to 37 are heirs of Tamim Golal. In order to resolve the dispute amongst the heirs they came to defendant No. l. Before commencing the proceeding defendant No.1 Chairman imposed a condition that he would mediate the dispute if they entrusted the entire land in his favour by a kabala deed. The plaintiffs in good faith did so, which is registered sale deed No.4995 dated 3.11.1988. 9/10 years have elapsed, but the Chairman did not settle the dispute among them. In September 1988 when they asked about arbitration, defendant No.1 Chairman became angry and replied that the land in question was returned to the defendant and on search they found three registered deed Nos.4217, 4218 and 4219 dated 03.09.1990. Defendant No.1 has no authority to execute the said kabala. Hence, the plaintiffs filed the suit.

4. Defendant No.1 contested the suit by filing a written statement contending, inter alia, that for the sake of settling the dispute among the heirs of Tamim Golal they sold out the entire land in his favour by registered sale deed No.4995 dated 03.11.1998. Actually, it was a trust deed. Until returning the land, he did not take possession of the land. A date of arbitration was fixed but he was not successful as nobody appeared. After sometime, they created pressure upon him to return the suit land and on the fixed date the plaintiffs did not come and the second party by creating pressure took the lands by registered sale deed Nos.4217-4219 dated 03.09.1990 which was not voluntarily given. He supported the plaint case and prayed for decreeing the suit.

5. The petitioner herein as defendant No.4 contested the suit by filing written statement denying all the material allegations contending, inter alia, that the schedule land originally belonged to his predecessor Mohammad Kalu. On 19.07.1952 Mohammad Kalu sold the entire land to his father Tamim Golal, who had two wives. He transferred 0.66 satak to his second wife Amirjan and her sons, namely Abu Hanifa and Mohammad Hanifa, and 0.40 satak land was sold to the petitioner's father Mohammad Kalu, Abu Hanifa, Mohammad Hanifa and Ashek Moula. After the death of Tamim his heirs inherited the remaining land. All the heirs of Tamim Golal on 23.11.1988 sold the entire land to defendant No.1 in consideration of money and delivered possession. Defendant No.1 by a registered sale deed No.4217 dated 03.09.1900 sold 1.87 sataks land to the petitioner's father Mohammd Kalu in consideration of money. For the purpose of reducing the registration cost, on the advice of the deed writer, the consideration was shown less than the paid amount. The petitioner's father was an illiterate and old man and as such defendant No.1 in connivance with the deed writer wrote some unnecessary statement in the deed which is beyond his knowledge, registered sale deed No.4217 dated 03.09.1990 is a saf-kabala and his father upon paying the proper consideration money acquired right, title and possession of the land. His father has been possessing the land by paying taxes etc. After the death of his father, the petitioner inherited the land. While in possession, he sold out 0.15 satak land to one Hashem Sawdagor. The remaining property was sold to defendant Nos.16-18 and they transferred the land to defendant No.38. All the heirs of Tamim Golal were acquainted with the said sale. Defendant No.1 is a rich and powerful man of the locality. On the other hand he had no courage to threat defendant No.l. It is not true that defendant No.1 was an arbitrator. Except the schedule land, Tamim Golal has more land but those were not included in the schedule. There is no Ekrarnama, no sitting or award. Defendant No.1 in connivance with some heirs of Tamim Golal instituted the suit; the written statement submitted by defendant No.1 is false. The heirs of Tamim Golal have no title, interest and possession in the suit land. After 23.11.1988 the price of the schedule land has increased thus, with a view to grab the land, they being greedy, instituted the suit after 9/10 years to test their luck, which is liable to be dismissed.

6. After hearing the parties and considering the materials on record, the Senior Assistant Judge, Chakaria, Cox's Bazar, by his judgment and decree dated 21.06.2001 decreed the suit. Being aggrieved, defendant No.4 preferred Title Appeal No.99 of 2001 in the Court of District Judge, Cox's Bazar. On transfer the said appeal was heard by the Joint District Judge, Second Court, Cox's Bazar, who after hearing the parties dismissed the appeal affirming the judgment and decree of the trial Court. Then the defendant filed Civil Revision No.4342 of 2010 before the High Court Division and obtained Rule, which upon hearing the parties was discharged. Hence, the defendant is now before us having filed the instant civil petition for leave to appeal.

7. Mr. A.S.M. Khalequzzaman, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submitted that the High Court Division erred in law in considering that the plaintiffs are the executants of the kabala in question and therefore very much party to the document and without a prayer for cancellation of the deed on payment of ad valorem court fees the suit for simple declaration is not maintainable and hence the impugned judgment and decree is liable to be set aside. He further submitted that the High Court Division and the Courts below concurrently committed an error in holding that the suit as filed on 04.01.1998 for declaration regarding the kabala No.4995 dated 23.11.1988 executed by the plaintiffs is not barred by the limitation and the simple suit for declaration without canceling the deed on payment of ad valorem court fees is not maintainable at all and hence the impugned judgment and decree is liable to be set aside. He submitted that the suit property is the homestead of the petitioner and the respondents in their respective shares pursuant to the kabala in question and the same is the only property of the petitioner and source of income for maintenance of the petitioner's family. The opposite party by taking a false plea has been trying to make the petitioner destitute. The trial Court utterly failed to appreciate the cunning device of the opposite party and has come to a wrong finding stating the kabala in question as jimma deed and as such the judgment and decree suffers from illegality and hence liable to be set aside.

8. Mrs. Quamrunnesa, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of respondent Nos.1, 2, 4-8 made submissions in support of the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division.

9. We have considered the submissions of the learned Advocates for the parties concerned, perused the impugned judgment and order and other connected papers on record.

10. We find from the judgment of the trial Court that upon considering all the evidence and materials it was concluded that the deed dated 23.11.1988 was not a deed of sale. In particular, it was noted that in that deed the quantum of land is written as 2.78 acres whereas D.W. 3 Ashek Ahmed, who is the only contesting defendant, admitted in is cross-examination that Tamim Golal had previously divested his title in respect of some of his land and he could have sold only 1.72 acres of the remaining land. The trial Court further noted that defendant No. 1 did not get possession of the land detailed in the deed dated 23.11.1988 and it was, therefore, not possible for him to transfer that land by way of the 3 deeds dated 03.09.1990. The trial Court concluded as follows:

“উক্তরুপে সাক্ষীদের সাক্ষ্য ও দাখিলীয় দলিল পর্যালোচনায় প্রমানিত হয় যে ৩-৯-৯০ ইং সনের ৪২১৭, ৪২১৮ ও ৪২১৯ নং কবলাগুলি ফেরত কবলা হয়। উহা বিক্রি কবলা নহে। উক্ত কবলায় টাকা পয়সা আদান প্রদান হয় নাই।”

11. The appellate Court being the last court of facts revisited the evidence and materials on record and noted that deed Nos. 4217, 4218 and 4219 of 1990-Ext.1- 1(Kha) disclosed in the body of those documents as follows:

“কষ্য নিদয় কবলা পত্র মিদং আগে যেহেতু নিম্ন তপসিলে বর্ণিত জমি জমা আমার বরাবরে গত ২৩/১১/৮৮ ইং তারিখ রেজিঃ যুক্ত ৪৯৯৮ নং কবলা মুলে বিচার নিষ্পত্তি করিয়া দেওয়ার জন্য রেজিষ্টি দিয়াছেন সে মতে আমার বিচার ও আপোষ নিষ্পত্তিতে আপনার হিংস্যাংশে প্রকৃত মূল্য ৩০০০/- সংখ্যা লিপি করিয়া উপস্থিত সাক্ষীগণের সম্মুখে অত্র কবলা দ্বারা আপনার নিকট অর্পন করিয়া চিরতরে অনুবলে সাবেক মতে দখল সূ্ত্রে স্বত্বাধিকারী থাকিয়া সন সন খাজনাদায়ে যদৃচ্ছা ভোগদখল দান ও বিক্রয় ইত্যাদি হস্তান্তর করিতে পারিবেন।”

12. The appellate Court also noted that deed No.4995/88- Ext-"P" shows a transfer of 2.78 acres of land whereas from the plaint and the written statement it is apparent that at the time the executants of the deed did not have 2.78 acres remaining in his possession. The appellate Court concluded that deed No. 4995/88 was a jimma deed not a deed of sale and defendant No. 1 did not take possession of the land in question and the deed was not effective. Consequently, deed Nos. 4217,4218 and 4219/90 executed by defendant No.1 were not sale deeds and no possession was handed over since the executants himself did not take possession of land in question by dint of deed No.4995/88.

13. The High Court Division noted that the appellate Court after elaborate discussion of the oral and documentary evidence independently found that defendant No. 1 never possessed the suit land. It was also observed that the appellate Court on perusal of the recital of the deeds found that the deed in favour of defendant No. 1 was a jimma deed for resolving the dispute between the parties.

<u>14. From the above discussion it transpires that the High Court Division upheld the concurrent findings of the Courts below. Clearly when the deeds under challenge contain in the recital that the earlier deed No.4995 dated 23.11.1988 was executed and registered only for the purpose of resolving the dispute through the intervention of defendant No.1, who was the Chairman of the Union Parishad that deed was not a sale deed. Hence, the deeds executed by the Chairman are equally not deeds of sale but simply return of the property. The later deeds disclose in no uncertain terms the nature of the transaction. Neither of the transactions, either in favour of or executed by the Chairman-defendant No.1 was a transfer involving sale of land. The Chairman was simply given land to hold in trust while he attempted to arbitrate the dispute between the parties. When he failed, he returned the land the Courts below rightly held that the deeds in question were not deeds of sale and no money changed hands. Accordingly, the deeds were not binding on the plaintiffs.</u>

15. In the light of the discussion above, we find that the impugned judgment and order does not suffer from any illegality or infirmity and does not call for any interference. Accordingly, the civil petition for leave to appeal is dismissed.

End.

lawyer:
Samiron Das Gupta, Advocate-For the Petitioner. 
Omar Farook, Advocate-For Opposite Party No.1.
parties:
Nasima Akhter Banu ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Abu Taher Masud and ors ------ Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
Syed Md Ziaul Karim J: This Rule, at the instance of plaintiff-petitioner, calls in question the legality and propriety of the order dated 24-4-2004 passed by the learned District Judge, Cox's Bazar in Civil Revision No. 13 of 2004 summarily rejecting the revisional application and affirming the order dated 10-3-2004 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Second Court, Cox's Bazar in Other Suit No. 39 of 1999/186 of 1994 rejecting the application filed under Order VI, rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure.

2. Short facts leading to this Rule are that on 27-8-1994 the petitioner as plaintiff instituted Partition Suit No. 186 of 1994 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Cox's Bazar against the defendants herein opposite parties, praying for a separate saharn of her share in the property for partition by metes and bounds Subsequently, the suit was transferred 'in the Second Court of Joint District Judge, Cox's Bazar wherein it was re-numbered as Partition Suit No. 39 of 1999.

3. The plaintiffs case, in brief, is that the suit land. originally belonged to Golam Nabi Sowdagar from whom she inherited her respective share in the suit property; that out of 4.28 acres of land of the disputed Khatian No. 1247 of 1977, Golam Nabi Sowdagar mortgaged 1.60 acres of land in favour of Abdus Salam and Nurul Islam by a registered mortgaged deed dated 7-5-1962, who were friends of him but possession was not delivered to them; that during old age of Go lam Nabi Sowdagar his son defendant-opposite party No.1, Abu Taher Masud was entrusted for management of the property who without redeeming 1.60 acres of land purchased the same in his own name; that the plaintiff and the defendants are the heirs of Golam Nabi Sowdagar and the plaintiffs being one of the daughter is entitled to have 0.21-1/4 acres of land by inheritance; that Golam Nabi Sowdagar died leaving behind two sons (defendant Nos. 1 and 2), five daughters (the plaintiff and the defendant Nos. 3-6) and one wife defendant No.7; and that defendant No.1 while refused to make partition of the suit land, the plaintiff filed the suit.

4. Defendant No.1 (herein opposite party No.1) appeared in the suit by filing written statement denying all the material allegations made in the plaint stating that he purchased 1.60 acres of land in the suit property from the heirs of Abdus Salam and Nurul Islam by different kabalas in 1985 and, as such, other heirs of Golam Nabi Sowdagar are not entitled to get share of the same and accordingly, prayed for separate saham

5. During pendency of the suit on 6-3-2003, plaintiff filed an application for amendment of the plaint seeking declaration that kabala Nos. 482 dated 17-1-1985,537 dated 19-1-1985,638 dated 24-1-1985, 692 dated 28-1-1985, 2698 dated 23-4-1985 and 3315 dated 1-6-1985 by which the defendant No.1 is said to have purchased the mortgaged land, are all collusive, illegal and void and not binding upon the plaintiff. The said application was allowed by the learned Joint District Judge on the same date.

6. Thereafter, on 20-8-2003 the plaintiff filed an application for amendment of the plaint under Order VI, rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure stating that due to inadvertence some amendment was done in the previous application dated 6-3-2003 which was not at all necessary, so he prayed for certain amendment relating to the prayer No. Ka(3) by which the plaintiff sought for a declaration that aforesaid kabalas of 1985 in the name of I the defendant No.1 are void, illegal and collusive and in its place it will be read that plaintiff and defendant Nos.1-7 accrued right, title, interest by those deeds.

7. Eventually the said application came up for hearing before the learned Joint District Judge, Second Court, Cox's Bazar who by the order dated 10-3-2004 rejected the same. Against which the plaintiff moved before the learned District Judge, Cox's Bazar in Civil Revision No. 13 of 2004 who by the order dated 24-4-2004 summarily rejected the same. Hence the Rule.

8. Mr Samiron Das Gupta, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner supports the Rule and submits that the learned District Judge misconceived the moot point in order to dispose of an application filed Under Order VI, rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure, thereby took erroneous  view, causing miscarriage of justice. He adds that the proposed amendment will not change the nature and character of the suit. He assails order of the learned Courts below by referring the Provisions laid down in Order VI, rule 17, CPC that to determine the real questions of controversy between the parties, at any stage of the proceedings the plaint may be amended. In support of his contention he referred the case of Md Sirajuddin vs Mahibunnesa and others reported in The Lawyers Volume 1 (AD) 136, wherein it is held:

"It is an established principle of law that the prayer of amendment can be allowed at any stage of the proceeding in order to decide the matter in controversy between the parties."

9. He further referred the case of Managing Committee NMC Model High School and others vs Obaidur Rahman reported in 31 DLR (AD) 133 wherein it is held:

"Amendment of the pleadings could be allowed at any stage of the proceedings for the purpose of determining the real question of controversy between the parties, but it could not be allowed if, it changed the nature and character of the suit or if the prayer for amendment had become barred by lapse of time and a right had accrued to the other side. One of the fundamental principles governing the amendment of the pleadings is that all the controversies between the parties as far as possible should be included and multiplicity of the proceedings avoided."

10. Mr Gupta lastly submits that the Courts below failed to weigh and sift the materials placed before them as required by law and evidently fell in an error in coming to their respective ultimate decision occasioning failure of justice.

11. Mr Omar Farook, the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party No.1, opposes the Rule and submits that once the plaintiff prayed for declaration that certain deeds mentioned in the application for amendment dated 6-3-2003 are illegal, inoperative and not binding upon her but by subsequent amendment she is claiming her right and title by those deeds, is not sound. In support of his contention, he referred the case of Nur Banu vs Noor Mohammad and others reported in 35 DLR (AD) 182 wherein it is held;

"A party cannot blow hot and cold in his stand before a Court of law."

12. Mr Farook lastly submits that considering materials on record the learned Courts below rightly rejected the prayer for proposed amendment. So, according to him, the impugned order calls for no interference by this Court.

13. We have gone through the plaint, the applications for amendment (Annexures B and D), impugned order and given our anxious considerations to the submissions advanced by the learned Advocates of both sides.

14. Now the question calls for our considerations whether the Court's below committed any error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in not allowing the application for amendment dated 20-8-2003.

15. For the convenience of understanding the provisions of Order VI, rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure reads as hereunder:

"Rule 17. The Court may at any stage of the proceedings allow either party to alter or amend his pleadings in such manner and on such terms as may be just and all such amendments shall be made as may be necessary for the purpose of determining the real questions in controversy between the parties."

16. It appears that the prayer Ka(3) of the plaint is in the following language:

আবদুছ ছালাম ও নুরুল ইসলামের ওয়ারীশ গণ হইতে ১নং বিবাদীর খরিদা ১৭-১-৮৫ইং, ১৯-১-৮৫ইং, ২৪-১-৮৫ইং, ২৮-১-৮৫ইং, ১-৬-৮৫ইং, ২৩-৪-৮৫ইং, তারিখের কবলাসমূহ ফেররী, বেআইনী যোগসাজসী এবং ভয়েড কবলা হওয়া ও তৎদ্বারা ১নং বিবাদী কোন স্বত্ব স্বার্থ ও দখল অর্জন করেন নাই এবং তৎদ্বারা বাদী ও নালিশী জমি বাধ্য নহে মর্মে ঘোষনার ডিক্রী দেওয়ায়ঃ

17. And by the proposed amendment petition dated, 20-8-2003, the above prayer, was sought to be changed in the following language-

আবদুছ ছালাম ও নুরুল ইসলামের ওয়ারিশগণ ইতে ১নং বিবাদীর খরিদা ১৭-১-৮৫ইং, ১৯-১-৮৫ইং, ২৪-১-৮৫ইং, ১-৬-৮৫ইং, ২৩-৪-৮৫ইং তারিখের কবলা সমূহ বাদীর পিতা গোলাম নবীর সওদাগরের কার্য্যকারক, এজেন্ট ও ট্রাষ্টি হিসেবে ১নং বিবাদীর নামীয় খারদা  এবং তাহাতে বাদী ও ১-৭ নং বিবাদী সকলের স্বত্ব স্বার্থ রহিয়াছে।

<u>18. We have considered the plaint and the application for proposed amendment and find that plaintiff instituted the suit for partition. The plaintiff and the defendant Nos.1-7 are the heirs of late Golam Nabi Sowdagar, It appears to us that the proposed amendment will in no way change the nature and character of the suit or substitute any cause of action rather the plaintiff wants to change the language of the prayer 3(ka) of the plaint for proper and complete adjudication of the suit which do not appear to be inconsistent, irrelevant, immaterial or contradictory to the facts of the plaint. We find that one of the fundament principles governing the amendment of the pleadings is that all the controversies between the parties as far as possible should be, included and multiplicity of the proceedings avoided.</u>

19. We like to observe that proposed amendment is necessary for the purpose, of determining the real questions in controversy between the parties and proper adjudication of the suit. Moreover, the plaintiff will prove his own case by adducing evidence and the defendants have the ample opportunity to file additional written statement against such amendment. The learned Joint District Judge by his order dated 10-3-2004 rejected the application on the following reasons:

একবার কোন দলিলকে অবৈধ বলিয়া দাবী করিয়া পরবর্তীতে সংশোধনীর মাধ্যমে ঐ দলিলের স্বত্বের উপর দাবী আনায়ন আইনানুগ ভাবে বিবেচনার গন্যে সংশোধনী প্রার্থনা সরাসরি নাকচ করা হয়।

<u>20. The aforesaid view is absolutely erroneous rather we find that the proposed amendment was explanatory and elucidative of facts already asserted in the plaint. The learned District Judge without considering the material facts and independent finding rejected the, revision and in consequence committed an error of law resulting in an erroneous decision occasioning failure of justice.</u>

21. In the case of Abdul Mutaleb vs Md Ershad Ali and others reported in 1998 BLD (AD) 121 = 4 BLC (AD) 150 it is held:

"Since all rules of the Court are intended to secure the proper administration of justice, it is essential that they should be made to serve and be subordinate to that purpose so that full powers of amendment may be enjoyed and, as such, it should always be liberally exercised The only limitation in allowing an amendment of the plaint is that the proposed amendment should not change the fundamental character and nature of the suit. The settled law is that amendment of pleadings may be allowed at any stage of the proceeding for the purpose of determining the real controversy between the parties."

22. This view also receives support in the cases of Md Khaledur Reza Chowdhury vs Saleha Begum and others reported in 1997 BLD (AD) 86 = 2 BLC (AD) 20, SN Roy Chowdhury vs A Jabber and others reported in 1994 BLD 229 = 46 DLR 273, Moyjuddin Mandai vs Bena Rani Das and others reported in 45 DLR 154 and MA Jahangir and others vs Abdul Malek and others reported in 41 DLR 389.

23. We are in respectful agreement with the principles enunciated in the cases reported in The Lawyers Vol. 1 (AD) 136 and 31 DLR (AD) 133 as referred by the learned Counsel for the petitioner and the same are applicable in this case but we failed to discover any merit in the submissions advanced by the learned Counsel for the opposite party No.1.

24. In view of the facts and circumstances of the case and foregoing narrative, we are led to the conclusion that the impugned order suffers from illegality and impropriety, occasioning failure of justice and calls for interference by this Court. Thus the Rule having merit succeeds.

25. In the result, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to cost. The application for amendment dated 20-8-2003 is allowed. The defendant No.1 is at liberty to file additional written statement against such amendment. The order of stay granted earlier by this Court is hereby vacated.

Communicate the order at once with a copy of the judgment for information and necessary action.

End.

lawyer:
Khandker Mahbubuddin Ahmed with Md Khalilur Rahman and Syeda Afsar Jahan, Advocates------ For the Petitioner. 
MA Mannan with Abdul Momen Chowdhury, Advocates------ For the Respondents.
parties:
Hotel Agrabad Ltd ------ Petitioner
vs
Chairman, Labour Court and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Syed Amrul Islam J: As common question of law and facts are involved in these Rules they were heard together and are being disposed of by this Judgment.

2. In these Rules the petitioner Company "Hotel Agrabad Ltd" (hereinafter called the petitioner Company) has called in question the judgment and order dated 31-12-91 passed in IRO Case Nos. 78 and 79 of 1984 by the First Labour Court, Chittagong whereby the learned Labour Court directed the Company to implement the scheme of the Companies Profits (Workers Participation) Act, 1968 in the petitioner Company.

3. Two sets of employees of the petitioner Company instituted IRO Case Nos. 78 and 79 of 1984 before the First Labour Court, Chittagong under sectiori 34 of the Industrial Relations Ordinance (hereinafter called IRO) for the enforcement of their rights as guaranteed to them by the Companies Profits (Workers Participation) Act, 1968 (hereinafter called the Act) contending that the petitioner company is an industrial undertaking within the meaning of the Act and fulfils all the conditions of the Act and, as such, must introduce the "scheme" as contemplated by section 2 of the Act. The case of the petitioner Company is that the Hotel Agrabad Ltd is not an industrial establishment within the meaning of the Act and, as such, the "scheme" does not apply to it and the case is not maintainable under section 34 of the IRO, inasmuch as no right is guaranteed to the respondents by or under any law.

4. The learned Labour Court on consideration of the materials and evidence on record by the impugned judgment found that there is no controversy between the parties over the use of electrical energy and machineries for making the rooms centrally air-conditioned. The learned Labour Court also found that the swimming pool and other amenities available in the hotel are also dependent on the use of electrical energy. It has also found that different items of food as per hotel menu is prepared in the kitchen by using electrical energy and in the bakery electrical energy is admittedly used for manufacture of bakery products of different kinds and thereby the value of the food is increased by changing the original condition. It is also found by the learned Labour Court that there is no dispute as to the fulfilment of the other conditions regarding number of workers, paid up capital, value of the fixed assets of the petitioner Company in order to attract the provisions of the aforesaid Act and, as such, found that the petitioner company comes within the definition of the industrial undertaking as contemplated in the said Act and thereby allowed the case of the respondent Nos. 2-47 and 2-60 of the respective cases.

5. Mr Khandker Mahbubuddin Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner company, submits that the hotel business may be termed as either establishment or enterprise as contemplated in the Act but he submits that in the explanation 'goods' means things which are consumed or used by human being and air is not a material nor goods, as such, in order to come within the definition of industrial undertaking, it must be found that goods or materials have been subjected either to any manufacturing or artificial process which changes the original condition or adds to their value. The learned Advocate further submits that adds to the value means increase in value and nothing else. The learned Advocate further submits that kitchen and bakery of a hotel can be termed as industrial undertaking but in the instant case the restaurant and the bakery had their own separate entity independent of the hotel itself and, as such, even if it is found that electrical energies are used to change the original condition of air by subjugation of it to artificial process that would not bring the Company's hotel business within the ambit of the Act. The learned Advocate further submits the since the word 'goods' and materials have not been defined in the Act the ordinary dictionary meanings of the words must be impugned to them. The learned Advocate finally submits that the hotel rooms or balconies do not come within the terms of goods or materials as contemplated in the Act and, as such, the Act has no manner of application to the petitioner company.

6. Mr MA Mannan, the learned Advocate appearing for the respondents, on the other hand, submits that it is not the hotel business only that is carried on by the petitioner company. If it is found that the petitioner company fulfils the condition as laid down in the Act then the Act will have its application in the instant case. The learned Advocate further submits that income of the petitioner company is derived from hotel business, attached restaurant and bakery shop and the laundry and it is admitted even by the petitioner Company that their restaurant and bakery shop is not open to the boarders and guests only but also to the outsiders and any member of public can go to the bakery shop or to the restaurant and buy any item of food manufactured by the petitioner company. The learned Advocate further submits that it is admitted that electrical energy is used in the kitchen and bakery shop for producing different items of food and also for maintaining certain level of temperature in all the rooms and the balconies including the swimming pool of the hotel and the temperature is cooled and maintained at a certain level by subjugation of normal air to an artificial process by the use of electrical energy. The learned Advocate further submits that it is also admitted by the parties that there is difference in rents between the air conditioned room and non-airconditioned room and admittedly the airconditioned room of the hotel is rented at a higher rate than the non-airconditioned room. Thus, the petitioner Company fulfilled all the requirements of the Act and, as such, they must introduce the scheme pursuant to the aforesaid Act for the benefit of the respondents and there is no illegality in the impugned judgment and the learned Labour Court taking a correct view of law and fact rightly passed the impugned judgment.

<u>7. We have perused the application and the affidavit-in-opposition and the papers annexed therewith and considered the submissions made by the learned Advocates of both the parties. We fully agree with the submission of Mr Ahmed that since the word 'goods' and materials have not been defined either in the Act or in the explanation appended to the scheme they will bear the ordinary dictionary meaning of the words. Goods, according to the Oxford Dictionary, means movable property, merchandise, Wares, things for transmission by. rail, etc. and merchandise means commodities of commerce, goods for sale and Materials means matter from which things are made as raw (unmanufactured) elements, constituent parts of substance, stuff, fabrics, etc. Here it should be noted the in the Act the word 'materials' has been used in its plural sense and air is a substance which consists of two elements, namely hydrogen and oxygen and with the combination of these, two elements the air is produced as substance. Thus it appears that when the petitioner company artificially controls the temperature of their rooms, balconies, ballroom and swimming pool they do it by subjugation of air to an artificial process by using electrical energy and thereby the amenities provided in the hotel is increased to a great extent for which they Can charge a high price from their customers, Besides, there is no dispute between the parties that, they use electrical energy in the kitchen and in the bakery shop for producing different items of food. It is also admitted that electrical energy is also used in the laundry for cleaning clothes, linens and other stuff and it is also admitted that by using the electrical energy certain, level of temperature is maintained in the swimming pool of the hotel. Here we may remember that the petitioner is Agrabad Hotel Ltd, a company incorporated under the Companies Act and they carry on the business of hotel wherein they provide the amenities as mentioned above and other modem amenities too, The Memorandum and Articles of Association is not before us but it is-admitted by both the parties that the petitioner company runs their hotel business along with bakery and restaurant within the same premises at Agrabad. Commercial Area within the port city of Chittagong and their profit and loss accounts is also maintained in the name of the Company. So, it is the Company who owns the entire establishment. Thus, we do not find any substance in the submission of Mr Ahmed that the restaurant and the bakery shop had their own independent entity independently of the petitioner Company. On a careful scrutiny of the scheme as appended to the schedule to the Act, it appears that when a company is involved in any operation where goods or materials are subjected to any manufacturing, finishing or other artificial process by using electrical energy to change their original conditions or to add to their value the Act is attracted and in the instant case, it is admitted position that the petitioner company uses electrical energy for producing different food items in the restaurant as well as different bakery items in the bakery shop by using electrical energy and also maintains a desired level of temperature in all the rooms including the restaurant and bakery shop by subjugation of air through artificial process for which the value of the foods and services rendered by the petitioner company is increased. It is true that the rooms and balconies of the hotel are not goods but the fact remains that by subjugation of air to an artificial process by using electrical energy the temperature inside the premises is maintained at a certain level as desired by the management of the petitioner company. It is this use of electric energy for subjugation of air to artificial process for running the air-condition plant brings the petitioner company within the ambit of the Act. Besides, by using electrical energy different food items are produced in the kitchen as well as in the bakery shop of the company. Electrical energy is also used in the laundry. Thus we find that the petitioner Company answers the description of "Industrial undertaking" within the meaning of the Act and we, therefore, do not find any illegality in the impugned judgment.</u>

8. Mr Ahmed half-heartedly argued that the IRO cases were not maintainable under section 34 of the IRO and the respondent employees ought to have filed an application under section 15 of the Payment of Wages Act, 1936. This submission is devoid of any substance.
