full_judgment:
Habibur Rahman Khan J: This appeal is directed against the judgment and decree dated 27.5.87 passed by Mr. Nurun Nabi Chowdhury, Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka, in Title Suit No. 103 of 1985 dismissing the suit on contest with cost.

2. The appellant Motiul Haque as plaintiff filed a suit for declaration with a prayer for a decree that the plaintiff has right, title and interest in the suit property measuring 10 kathas I chhatak of land situated in the Gulshan Model Town being plot No. 22 of Block CWs(B).

The facts of the case, in short, are as follows: The plaintiff being a national of Bangladesh proposed to take and the defendant No. 1 Dhaka Improvement Trust now RAJUK, agreed to give lease of 10 kathas I chhatak of land at Gulshan Model Town in Dhaka in consideration of the payment of Taka 8,154/- for the purpose of erecting a residential house by the plaintiff, for a period of 99 years commencing from the 30th day of October, 1962 and pursuant to that agreement and for consideration of Tk. 8,154/- paid in full by the plaintiff, the defendant No. 1 executed a proper conveyance deed under caption "Standard lease agreement for land" executed on the 21st March, 1968 which was registered on 17th April, 1968 between the defendant No. 1 as lessor and the plaintiff as lessee accompanied by delivery of possession of the suit land on the terms and conditions and warranties embodied in the deed. According to terms mentioned in the deed, the lessee was to complete the construction of the building on the demised property for the purpose of residence getting the plan approved by the DIT within 4 years. It was also stipulated that if the lessee fails to complete the construction within 4 years he shall surrender the demised property to the lessor forthwith and the amount paid by him on account of the premium will be returned to him. The lease having commenced from the 30th day of October, 1962 the period of 4 years have long come to an end on 30th day of October, 1966 but the defendant No. 1 have not exercised its right, if any had, under the clause 5, nor the plaintiff prayed for extension of the period beyond 4 years. During the war of liberation in 1971 the plaintiff had to give up his place of residence at 13/12, Babar Road, Mohammadpur, Dhaka and moved from one place to another for his residence. The plaintiff met with accident in 1973 and his left leg was broken and there was little hope of his survival and hence he entrusted his close friend Syed Mohammad Anwar Hossain with the management of the property. The plaintiff partially recovered from illness in May-June, 1980 but as he was unable to move freely he engaged his relation Mr. Nawshad Noori to look after the suit property. In July, 1980 the said Nawshad Noori informed the plaintiff that some persons went to take delivery of possession of the suit property on the basis of some decree from Civil Court against the plaintiff. The plaintiff got information that Mrs. Momtaz Begum, wife of Syed Mohammad Anwar Hossain, has obtained a decree in Title suit No. 276 of 1974 of the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka. The plaintiff filed Misc. Case No. 173 of 1980 in the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka for setting aside the ex parte decree obtained against him by suppressing summons. The decree was ultimately set aside and the Title Suit No. 276 of 1974 was restored to its original file and number. The suit was, however, 'ultimately dismissed on compromise on 29.3.81.

3. The plaintiff wrote to the defendant No. 1 about the aforesaid affairs and thereafter submitted a plan on 19.8.1990 for the construction of residential house on the suit property. The plaintiff also sent reminder to the defendant No. 1. Thereafter a reply being Memo No. DIT/430-F dated 12.2.1981 was sent by the defendant No. 1 to the plaintiff at his address at 25/27 Tajmahal Road. Block-C Mohammadpur, Dhaka, but the said letter was not delivered to him because there was change of his address. In the meantime coming to know about the said letter plaintiff approached the defendant No. 1 to send a copy of the aforesaid undelivered letter. Ultimately the said letter was sent along with the letter dated 12.2.81 vide Memo No. DIT/ED/69 dated 9.4.81 which was received by the plaintiff on the same date. By the said memo the plaintiff ' informed by the defendant that the plaintiffs lease o the demised property was determined as per clause 5 of the lease deed under defendant's memo No. DIT/ABO(E) 655-1 dated 30.1.75 due to his failure in constructing the building within the stipulated time. Further case of the plaintiff was that he did not receive the alleged notice dated 30.1.75, nor did he receive any show cause notice before the alleged termination of the lease. It is also alleged that the defendants have not instituted any suit to recover the suit property, nor paid the sum of Taka 8,154.00 being the consideration money which was paid by the plaintiff to the defendant No. 1. It is asserted that the plaintiff having not surrendered the demised property the plaintiff is still in physical possession and enjoyment of the said property. In the suit the plaintiff has also challenged the notice under memo No. DIT/AED(N)-655-P dated 301.75 as being illegal and not binding upon the plaintiff and as such it has not affected the right, title, interest and possession of the plaintiff over the suit property. But as it has cast a cloud over the title of the plaintiff in the suit property he has been compelled to file the suit.

4. The defendant No. 1 challenged the claim of the plaintiff by filing written statement stating, inter alia, that the suit is not maintainable against the defendant at such a belated stage, the suit is hopelessly barred by limitation and by the principle of estoppel, waiver and acquiescence, the notice dated 30.1.75 terminating the lease was sent to the given address of the plaintiff and as such the defendant discharged their legal obligation. It is asserted in the written statement that the plaintiff took lease of the property from the defendant No. 1 by executing a standard lease deed on 21st March, 1968 which was later on registered on 19.4.68. The plaintiff was required to abide by the rules, regulations, by-laws and the terms and conditions of the said deed. The plaintiff having failed to comply with the terms and conditions embodied in clause 4 of the deed the defendant terminated the lease in accordance with the terms and conditions laid down in clause 5 of the deed of lease. It is also asserted that the lease with the plaintiff has been determined in a regular way and in accordance with the terms and conditions embodied in the lease deed.

5. Mr. MI Faroqui, the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff appellant and Mr. Ziaur Rahman Khan, the learned Advocate appearing for the defendant Dhaka Improvement Trust (now RAJUK), made their respective submissions in the appeal. Though a number of grounds have been taken in the memo of appeal, Mr. Farooqui has strenuously argued laying stress only on a few of them after taking us through the plaint, written statement, the deposition of the witnesses and the documents produced and marked as exhibits in the suit and also the judgment of the learned Trial Court. The most important material in the case is the lease deed a copy of which has been marked Ext. 1 as produced by the plaintiff and Ext. 'C' as produced by the defendant. The said lease deed dated 21.3.68 contains 32 clauses in the nature of terms and conditions for the guidance of the respective parties in the deed. Out of them clauses 4, 5, 27, 30 and 32 are relevant for the purpose of adjudication of the dispute arising between the parties in the suit. The clause 4 of the lease deed runs as follows:

"That within four years from the date of commencement of the lease or within such further time as the lessor may allow in their discretion, the lessee shall complete the construction on the demised property of a building with all necessary out houses, boundary marks, drains and appurtenances for the purpose of residence including a septic tank of a pattern approved by the Authorised Officer of the Dacca Improvement Trust."

6. What will happen in case of failure on the part of the lessee in complying with the above terms has been provided in clause 5 of the deed which runs as follows :

"That if the lessee fails to complete the building of such house, out house, appurtenance within the period referred to in clause 5; the lease shall be liable to be terminated by the lessor and on such termination the lessee shall surrender the demised property to the lessor forthwith and the lessor shall refund to the lessee the actual amount paid on account of premium, but the lessee shall never-the-less be liable to pay rent at the stipulated rate for the period of the lease period up to the date of its termination, part of a year being counted as a full year for the purpose of the payment of such rent."

7. The above quoted two clauses as embodied in the Ext. 1 (Ext-A) cast upon the lessee an obligation on mutual agreement to complete the construction of the building within 4 years from the commencement of the lease. Clause 5 gives right to the lessor to terminate the lease on the lessee's failure to complete the building, etc. within the stipulated time, unless found to have been extended by the lessor, and on such termination it was a duty on the part of the lessee to surrender the demised property forthwith and on such termination, if followed by surrender, the lessor was obliged to pay back the amount of the consideration money to the lessee.

8. In the suit the following issues were framed for determination :

"1) Whether the suit is maintainable in its present form and manner?

2) Whether the suit is properly valued and Court fees paid is sufficient?

3) Is the suit bad for defect of parties?

4) Is the suit barred by limitation, estoppel, waiver and acquiescence?

5) Is the plaintiff entitled to get the relief prayed for?

6) What other or further relief or reliefs the plaintiff, in law and equity, is entitled to?"

9. In support of his case the plaintiff Md. Motiul Hoque examined himself as PW 1. On behalf of defendant, Taiful Alam, the manager of RAJUK was examined as DW. Both the parties have produced a number of documents which were marked as Exts. 1-10(B) from the plaintiff's side and Exhibits A-C from the defendant's side.

<u>10. The learned trial Court on consideration of the evidence, both oral and documentary, by his judgment and decree dismissed the suit with cost. Being aggrieved, the plaintiff preferred the instant appeal before this Court. Except issue Nos. 2 and 3 all issues were found against the plaintiff by the trial Court. Mr. Farooqui submits that the finding of the learned trial Court with regard to the maintainability is erroneous inasmuch as the jurisdiction of the Civil Court cannot be said to have been ousted by agreement unless it is specifically barred by any law and for that matter the terms of the agreement to the extent of barring tile jurisdiction of the Court is void. It is now well settled that the ouster of Court's jurisdiction is not to be readily inferred and even when there is an express ouster of Court's jurisdiction the Court shall retain its jurisdiction unless the order passed is without jurisdiction or malafide or not in accordance with law. In the case of Messers Chalna Fibre Company, Ltd. and 4 others Vs. Abdul Jabbar and 9 others reported in 20 DLR (SC) 335 it was held that normally a suit which is of civil nature is tribal by the Civil Court under section 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure unless it is found expressly or impliedly barred. In the instant case there is nothing to show that the suit is specifically barred by any law or enactment or there has been an ouster of Court's jurisdiction by any law expressed or implied and, therefore, we are of the view that the learned trial Court has erred in law in arriving at a finding that that the suit is not maintainable.</u>

11. The basis of the claim of the plaintiff is the lease deed Ext. 1 which was executed between the plaintiff and the defendant on 21.3.68 consequent on which delivery of possession of the suit property was given to the plaintiff on payment of the entire amount of the premium. The plaintiff has called in question the order of forfeiture of the suit land by the defendant for not completing the construction of the building in compliance with the terms of the deed. The plaintiff has not asserted that the terms of the deed of lease was in any way unconscionable, illegal or against public policy. The plaintiff's grievance is that the lease has not been determined legally in support of which the learned Advocate for the appellant has argued that no notice was issued and served upon the plaintiff giving him the time and opportunity to comply with the terms under clause 4 of the lease deed and the impugned notice terminating the lease could not be deemed to have been served on the plaintiff and such notice was never tendered to the plaintiff. From the fact that the defendant has not made any re-entry in the demised property it is argued that for non-compliance of the provision of he terms as embodied in clause 27 of the deed and floss the provision of 111(g) and 114A of the Transfer of Property Act and that the plaintiff is still folding the land in his possession, the order of determination of lease suffers from legal infirmities. The learned Advocate further submits that according D the terms of the deed the notice must be of the duration of one calendar month and such notice shall be deemed to have been served on the lessee, if I addressed to him on the demised property or forwarded to him by post or left at his last known address and a notice sent by post shall be deemed to be given at the time when in due course of post it would be delivered at the address to which it is sent. It was also stipulated that after the service of notice the lessor shall re-enter upon the whole of the demised property vide clause 27 of the deed and the lessor shall return to the lessee the actual amount paid on account of the premium vide clause 4 of the deed. The learned Advocate further submits that if all the above procedures are followed in compliance of the provision of the lease deed and the provision of law as well, then and then only property shall vest wholly in the lessor whereupon the lessor shall be the absolute owner of the property but in the instant case there being no substantial compliance of clauses 27 and 30 of the lease deed so far as it relates to the service of notice in writing and taking over possession of the property by the defendant by way of re-entering into the demised property, the lease has not been determined and the demised property has not become the property of the lessor. The learned Advocate reiterates that the lease has not been determined and forfeiture is not complete in view of the fact that no notice was served on the demised premises and the registered notice said to have been issued could not be treated as a good service as the same was returned to the sender with the endorsement 'not known' by the postal peon.

12. Mr. Zia-ur-Rahman Khan, the learned Advocate appearing for the defendant No. 1 'RAJUK', submits that all the procedures as embodied in the lease deed having been strictly followed and the provision of section 111(g) having been complied with the lease has been determined and with the determination of the lease the lessee has ceased to ,have any right over the demised property. With regard to the notice the learned Advocate for the respondent submits that since the notice issued by registered post to the plaintiff was properly addressed to his last known place of residence and was returned to the sender with the endorsement 'not known' by the postal peon, it shall be deemed as good service. From the pleadings and evidence adduced by respective parties the admitted position is as follows: Consequent on the allotment a bilateral lease deed was executed by the plaintiff as lessee and the DIT (now RAJUK) as lessor on 21.3.68 in respect of 30 kathas of land in Gulshan Model Town (demised property) and accordingly the possession was delivered to the lessee. In the lease deed the address of the lessee was given as 13/12 Babar Road PS Mohammadpur. There is specific term embodied in clause 4 of the deed that the lessee shall complete the construction on the demised property a building with all necessary out house, boundary, etc. within 4 years from the commencement of the lease or within such further time as the lessor may allow in his discretion with the approval of the DIT and if the lessee fails to complete the construction the lease shall be liable to be terminated by the lessor and on such termination the lessee shall surrender the demised property to the lessor forthwith. The plaintiff has not surrendered the possession of the said property to the defendant and the defendant has also not tendered the sum of Taka 8,154.00 to the plaintiff and the plaintiff has still been in possession of the property and the defendants have also not taken any step for the recovery of possession.

13. The dispute arose when the plaintiff submitted a plan for the construction of a residential house on the suit property to the defendant No. 1 on 19.8.80 and thereafter the reminder was sent by the defendant vide memo No. DIT/430-F dated 12.2.81 which was communicated to the plaintiff on 10.4.81 vide memo No. DIT/EC/1269-F dated 9.4.81 with the information that the lease of the suit property has been determined as per clause 5 of the lease deed under their notice No. DIT/AEO/(F)-665-P dated 30.1.74 due to the failure of the plaintiff in constructing the building in compliance of the terms of the lease deed. It is contended that the plaintiff was not served with any notice to show cause before the alleged termination of lease by the defendant No. 1, nor did he receive the notice under memo No. DIT/AEO/(E) 655-P dated 30.1.75 determining the lease. It is further contended that the notice being No. DIT/AEO(E)-655-P dated 30.1.75 is illegal and not binding upon the plaintiff and it has not affected the right, title, interest and possession of the plaintiff over the suit property but it has cast a cloud over the title of the plaintiff for which the suit has been filed. The plaintiff as PW admitted the provision of clause 4 in his deposition saying." In clause 4 of the lease deed a period of four years was mentioned for completing the construction of the suit property and the said four years expired on 30.10.66. Neither the defendant No. 1 invoked clause 5 of the lease deed nor I ever prayed for extension of the period. The property is in my possession." The plaintiff has tried to make out a case that he had to leave his place of residence at 13/12 Babar Road, Mohammadpur and moved from place to place and in 1973 he met with an accident and his left leg was broken. As he could not move freely he had to engage his relation Nowshad Nuri to look after his property. In July, 1980 he was informed that some persons went to take possession of the property on the basis of a decree obtained by Mrs. Momtaz Begum, wife of Anwar Hossain, his one time close friend. The suit having been restored was ultimately dismissed on compromise by 1st Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka. Thereafter the plaintiff submitted a plan with requisite fees on 2.9.80 whereupon the plaintiff was informed by the DIT that the lease was determined as per clause 5 of the lease deed for not constructing any building within the stipulated time and an intimation was sent to the plaintiff on 30.1.75. The plaintiff asserts that he did not surrender possession of the property to the defendant No. 1 or to anyone else and that he has still been in possession of the suit property. He also stated that on 1.3.75 the defendant No. 1 published a news in Bangladesh Observer under the caption 'DIT LEASE HOLDER' asking them to start construction. In reply to cross-examination he admitted that he did not make any construction on the suit land as per clause 4 of the lease agreement. He did not pray for extension of time for construction. His residential address was 13/12 Babar Road, Mohammadpur. He did not inform the DIT about the change of his address. The plaintiffs claim is that his right, title and interest in the suit property has not been affected by defendant No. 1's memo DIT/C(N) 655-P dated 30.1.75.

14. The DW 1 who deposed on behalf of defendant No. 1 also filed the deed of agreement Ext. C which corresponds to Ext. 1. It is stated that the plaintiff violated the terms of lease as embodied in clauses 4 and 5 of the lease deed. The show cause notice was issued on 11.8.70 (Ext. B) and not getting any reply the letter determining the lease was sent on 30.1.75 under registered cover Ext. C and C (I). He denied the defence suggestion that clauses 4 and 5 were not conditions but warranties.

15. Now let us deal with the point regarding the service of notice on the plaintiff terminating his lease. The lease is said to have been determined by a letter of the defendant No. 1 on 30.1.75 vide Ext. C. Mr. Farooqui argues the though the letter was shown to have been served on the plaintiff he could not have been imputed with the knowledge of the same unless it could be shown that the notice was tendered to or thereafter either received or returned being refused by the addressee. It is also argued that there cannot be any presumption of service of notice when the notice is found to have been returned with the endorsement 'not known' by the postal peon on the registered cover containing the notice. The learned Advocate also submits that after the liberation war period the plaintiff had to move from one place to another for his residence and, therefore, the return of the letter to the sender with the endorsement 'not known' cannot be treated as a good service and the plaintiff cannot be said to have knowledge of the forfeiture of his lease hold interest in the suit land. Mr. Zia-ur-Rahman Khan by way of referring to the section 27 of the General Clauses Act submits that the registered notice sent by post carries with it. the strong presumption of service of same if the notice is properly addressed and posted, unless this presumption is rebutted by cogent evidence. He submits that in the instant case the notice was admittedly issued by registered post with proper address but the presumption of due service was not rebutted as the notice was found to have been returned to the addressee with the endorsement Not know', by the postal peon. The provision of section 27 of the General Clauses Act which is relevant for the purpose reads as follows:

"Meaning of service by post. Where any Act of Parliament or Regulation made after the commencement of this Act authorises or requires any document to be served by post, whether the expression" serve" or either of the expressions "give" or "send" or any other expression is used, then, unless a different intention appears, the service shall be deemed to be effected by properly addressing, pre-paying and posting by registered post, a letter containing the document, and, unless the contrary is proved, to have been effected at the time at which the letter would be delivered in the ordinary course of post."

<u>16. Mr. Zia-ur-Rahman Khan has referred to he case of Alauddin Vs. Md. Idris Mia decided by a Tingle Bench of this court and reported in 22 DLR 664 wherein it is held:</u>

<u>"It is true that the presumption raised by section 27 of the General Clauses Act, 1897 is a rebuttable one. But a mere denial to the effect that the notice was not received by him is not sufficient to rebut the presumption" and "Notice sent by registered post returned with the endorsement 'Left' on the registered cover by the postman although at the material time the addressee was residing at the particular address—presumption is that the notice was duly tendered to the addressee and the addressee must be fixed with constructive notice."</u>

<u>In the said case reliance was placed on the case of Monomohen Ray Choudhury Vs. Ajit Kamal Dutta Gupta reported in 6 DLR 267 and the case of Hari Pada Dutta Vs. Jay Copal Mukherji reported in 39 CWN 934 wherein his Lordship Rankin CJ sitting with Person J, Held :</u>

<u>"That a summons sent by registered post and returned with the endorsement 'refused' is prima facie evidence that the addressee had an opportunity to accept it and the service thus effected is, therefore, a good and valid service and that to invalidate such a service the defendant must expressly prove to the satisfaction of the Court, that what would happen in the ordinary course did not happen and that he did not get any opportunity to accept it, and for that purpose it is open to him to prove that he never refused it and that it was never tendered to him, and that a mere denial that it was never delivered to him is not sufficient."</u>

17. Thus we find that if a letter is found posted and correctly addressed and returned being found to have been refused it has been held as good service in a number of cases of the superior courts of this country and those of Indian jurisdiction. But what will be the position if the letter is returned to the sender with the endorsement either 'left' or with the endorsement 'not known' as in the present case, is the point to which our attention has been drawn.

18. In the case of Sita Nath Mandal Vs. Soleman Molla and others reported in 51 CWN 650 it is held:

"The endorsement 'left' on the registered cover in the opinion of the learned Judge, is of no value where it is proved that at the material time the defendant was residing at the residential address given on the cover of the registered notice and that under such circumstances it must be taken that the notice was duly tendered to the defendant and the service was complete notwithstanding the endorsement 'left'."

19. In the agreement the address of the plaintiff was given as 13/12 Babar Road, Mohammadpur and there is nothing to show that the change of address was ever communicated to the defendant by the plaintiff. Furthermore, Ext. 10A the affidavit sworn by plaintiff on 13.3.72 shows that the plaintiff was residing at 13/12 Babar Road, Mohammadpur and the affidavit Ext. 10(B) contains averment that the plaintiff had been carrying on his contract business under the name and style M/S. Northern Construction with its head office at 13/12 Babar Road, Mohammadpur, Dhaka. Thus there is no scope for making any inference that the plaintiff was not residing and was also not available there at 13/12 Babar Road, Mohammadpur as mentioned or that there was any change of the address given by him in the deed.

<u>20. In the case of Dr. Jamshed Bakht Vs. Md. Kamaluddin reported in 1981 BO) 97 it was held that mere denial of receipt of the notice by the addressee or that the notice was not tendered to him is not sufficient to rebut the presumption of the service of notice by registered post as provided in section 27 of the General Clauses Act. The fact that the address of the plaintiff was given in the deed of lease as 13/12 Babar Road, Mohammadpur which also finds support from the subsequent affidavit sworn by the plaintiff vide Ext. 10(a) 10(b) and the plaintiff having not ever intimated about the change of his address leads us to the presumption that 13/12 Babar Road was the address of the plaintiff and this presumption having not been rebutted in any way by the defendant we are of view that the notice under registered cover was sent and properly addressed to the plaintiff. Though there is minor factual difference between the case where the notice under registered cover was returned to the sender with the endorsement 'left' and the present case where a letter under registered cover has been returned with the endorsement 'not known' by the postal peon the nature, intention and purpose, the mode applied and the effect in both the cases are virtually the same so far it relates to the service of notice. As we have already found from the record that the letter was properly addressed and the cover containing the notice was sent by registered post to the plaintiff to his address given by himself in the deed of agreement by the plaintiff and the said place of residence of the plaintiff being his last known place of residence, we hold that the presumption arises that the notice was duly tendered to the addressee and the said presumption having not been rebutted the addressee must be fixed with constructive notice.</u>

21. Now let us see whether there has been compliance of the provision of sections 111(g) and 114A of the Transfer of Property Act. Section 111 (g) Provides—

"by forfeiture; that is to say, (1) in case the lessee breaks an express condition which provides that on breach thereof the lessor may re-enter or (2) in case the lessee renounces his character as such by setting up a title in a third person or by claiming title in himself, or (3) the lessee is adjudicated an insolvent and the lease provides that the lessor may re-enter on the happening of such event and in any of these cases the lessor or his transferee gives notice in writing to the lessee of his intention to determine the lease."

Section 114A provides:

"Where a lease of immovable property has been determined by forfeiture for a breach of an express condition which provides that on breach thereof the lessor may re-enter, no suit for ejectment shall lie unless and until the lessor has served on the lessee a notice in writing (a) specifying the particular breach complained of and (b) if the breach is capable of remedy, requiring the lessee to remedy the breach; and the lessee fails, within a reasonable time from the date of the service of the notice, to remedy the breach, if it is capable of remedy.

Nothing in this section shall apply to an express condition against the assigning, under letting, parting with the possession or disposing of the property leased, or to an express condition relating to forfeiture in case of non-payment of rent."

22. Mr. MI Farooqui submits that if lease of immovable property is determined by forfeiture, that is to say on the breach of an express condition, the lessor may re-enter and, therefore, unless there is such condition and breach thereof and there is compliance of the provision of section 114A of the Transfer of Property Act the lessor cannot get back and hold the property absolutely. In support of his contention the learned Advocate has placed before us the case of Bangladesh and another Vs. M/s. ATJ Industries Ltd. and others reported in 29 DLR (SC) 181 wherein it is held that unilateral cancellation of the lease by the government cannot be a ground for dispossessing the company. from the demised property by the application of force.

23. In the case before us the dispute has not arisen out of the action of the lessor taking forcible possession of the demised property but it relates to the determination of the lease for the breach of condition embodied in the lease deed. There being substantial compliance of the provision of 111(g) of the Transfer of Property Act and the question relating to compliancy of the provision of section 114A of the Transfer of Property Act having not arisen as yet the case cited before us is of no assistance to the plaintiff. The learned Advocate for the appellant has also cited the case of Dooni Lai Seal and another Vs. Smt. Giniya Doti Rateria and others reported in AIR 1970 (Cal) 452 wherein it is held :

"Section 114A should be so reasonably constructed and in such a manner that an effective meaning could be attached to it. The question that has to be answered is whether the lessor after determining the lease could ask for rent during the period of notice. There is no reason why the lessor cannot ask the lessee to pay the rent in the meantime. There can be no point in asking the lessee to remedy the breach and at the same time asking him to pay the occupation charges as compensation or damages or as manse profits, more so, when by the statute itself the lessor has no right to file any suit without giving the lessee reasonable chance to remedy the breach. There is no provision for waiver or forfeiture as contemplated under section 114A. Where the breach complained of is capable of remedy the notice must be in accordance with section 114A read with section 111, clause (g). The notice must not only specify the breach but also give reasonable time to the lessee who is called upon to remedy the breach within such reasonable time. It is the, and then only the cause of action to file a suit for eviction by the lessor against the lessee would arise. In such a case if the said provision is not complied with then the suit by lessor would become barred because the notice would be bad in law. Until the expiry of the notice under section 114A the lessor would claim not manse profit but rent for the said period in the case of section 114A. It is not relief in that sense that is granted but the forfeiture itself does not become operative until the expiry of the reasonable period mentioned in the notice. The relief is granted by allowing the lessee some time to remedy the breach by keeping the forfeiture in abeyance."

24. In the case of section 114A it would no doubt be provided in the notice an expression such as "the lessor hereby determines the lease" but the meaning that has to be attached to the said expression and the effect thereof is that the forfeiture would take effect not from the date of notice but upon the failure of the lessee to remedy the breach within the time reasonably granted by the notice.

25. In the case cited the lessor filed a suit for taking possession of the lease-hold property after determination of the lease and in the instant case the lease was determined by the lessor on the breach of conditions by the lessee as embodied in the lease deed and issuing notice on him determining the lease invoking the aid of clause 5 of the lease deed and also the provision of section 111(g) of the Transfer of Property Act and, therefore, we find that the principle laid down in the case under reference is not applicable in the present case.

26. Mr. MI Farooqui further submits that the land having been allotted to the plaintiff-appellant on payment of the entire lease money the possession of the same was delivered to him but he could not make construction in compliance of the clause 4 of the deed of lease due to the circumstances beyond his control. He had to keep himself away for some time after the liberation of Bangladesh for his own safety. Thereafter, he met with an accident and was also involved in some litigation with others over the suit property. After his recovery and being relieved of the anxieties he approached the DIT by way of submitting plan for making the construction and came to learn that his lease was cancelled and determined on 30.1.75. The grounds for none compliance of the terms and conditions of the lease deed which resulted in the forfeiture of the lease does not appeal to us as reasonable because of the long lapse of time. The aced was executed and registered on 21.3.68 and 17.4.68 respectively and the prayer for approval of the plan was made by the plaintiff on 2.9.90 and during this long period the, appellant was in deep sleep to think about and assert his own right over the suit property. After about 13 years suddenly on one fine morning he woke up from his slumber and discovered that he has a property at Gulshan where he was required to construct a building. We find no satisfactory explanation for such an unusual delay although he was supposed to be fully aware of his right and responsibility as contained in the lease deed which binds him to perform his part of the obligation as mentioned in the deed of lease. We do not find anything wrong in the acts of the lessor-defendant in determining the lease invoking the aid of clauses 4 and 5 of the lease deed.

27. Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and evidence on record we find that the plaintiff is not entitled to the decree as prayed for.

In the result, the appeal is dismissed without any order as to costs and the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court is hereby affirmed.

End.

full_judgment:
Tariq-ul-Hakim J : This Rule Nisi has been issued on an application under Article 102 of the Constitution by the Petitioner calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the impugned Memo No.16.02.0000.05.031.396.57/ 273(1-4) dated 1-8-2016 issued by the respondent No. 3 and notification published in the Daily Azadi on 4-8-2016, appointing respondent No. 4 Mutawalli in violation of the waqf deed and the waqf Ordinance, 1962 as evidenced by Annexure A and A(1) respectively should not be declared to have been issued and published without lawful authority and of no legal effect and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

2. The case of the Petitioner is that late Haji Abdul Gani Saudagor by registered deed Nos. 857 and 2342 dated 8-10-1945 and 16-3-1947 respectively donated all his property for creating a Waqf and Awlad. In the said deeds Mr Saudagar stated that he would be the Mutwalli of the said waqf estate until his death and after his death if he does not have any son or daughter, his brother's son Danu Miah will be the Mutawalli. It was further stated in the said deed that after the death of Danu Miah his eldest son Jamaluddin Khan will be the Mutawalli. In clause 1 of the Waqf Deed it was further stated that the said Jamaluddin Khan will appoint a Mutawalli before his death who will take his place after his death. Likewise each Mutawalli will appoint a Mutawalli to succeed him after his death.

3. Mr Saudagar died on 16-11-1973 leaving behind no son or daughter. In accordance with Clause 1 of the aforesaid Waqf Deed therefore his brother's son Danu Mia became the Mutawalli. Danu Mia died leaving behind four sons (1) Jamaluddin Khan (2) Md Feroz Khan (3) Md Saifuddin Khan and (4) Md Azizuddin Khan and four daughters. After the death of Danu Miah Jamaluddin Khan became Mutawalli in accordance with Clause 1 of the said Waqf Deed. It is stated that the said Jamaluddin Khan vide registered deed dated 10-3-2004 appointed the petitioner Mutwalli after his death as per Clause 1 of the said Waqf Deed subject to his attaining the age of majority by then. The petitioner attained the age of majority on 15-3-2011 and since then he has been acting as Mutawalli on behalf of his father Jamaluddin Khan died on 16-5-2016 leaving behind his wife, one son and nine daughters. Before the death of Jamaluddin Khan, the respondent No. 4 on 9-7-2007 filed an application under section 32(1) of the Waqf Ordinance, 1962 for removing Jamaluddin Khan from the office of Mutawalli. The said application was however filed after Jamaluddin Khan had been acting as Mutawalli for 20 years. After the death of Jamaluddin Khan on 16-5-2016, the respondent No. 4, a brother of late Jamaluddin Khan, by an application dated 22-5-2016 applied to the Respondent No.2 to be appointed Mutawalli. On the same date another brother of Jamaluddin Khan one Azizuddin Khan and a sister Anowara Khanam by two separate applications both dated 22-5-2016 also applied for being appointed Mutawalli. The petitioner by his letter dated 25-5-2016 (received on 31-5-2016) also made an application to the respondent No.2 Administrator of Waqf enclosing a copy of the registered Deed dated 10-3-2004 for being appointed Mutawalli. Respondent No. 3 after hearing all the applicants vide the impugned order appointed the respondent No.4 as official Mutawalli of the waqf estate for a period of 5 years under section 44 of the Waqf Ordinance, 1962.

Being aggrieved, the petitioner has come to this Court and obtained the present Rule.

4. The Rule is being contested by the Respondent No.4 by filing Affidavit-in-Opposition stating inter alia that the last Mutawalli Jamaluddin Khan violated the terms and conditions of the original Waqf deeds dated 8-10-1945 and 13-6-1947 registration Nos. 857 and 2342 respectively. It is alleged that Jamaluddin Khan on 10-3-2004 before his death created a new deed extinguishing and destroying the purpose of the original Waqf Deeds and the intention of the waqif. The deed created on 10-3-2004 by the last Mutawalli Jamaluddin Khan is not sustainable in law because it was not made in accordance with the original Waqf Deeds but is a new Waqf deed. The last Mutawalli Jamaluddin Khan by his deed dated 10-3-2004 travelled beyond the intention of the waqif and the original purpose of the Waqf Deed and therefore it is illegal and void. It is further stated that a Mutawalli has no power to appoint his successor during his life time and that such appointment can only be made on his death. The respondent No.4 filed an application to the Administrator of Waqf on 9-7-2007 under section 32(1) of the Waqf Ordinance, 1962 for removal of the then Mutawalli on the ground of breach of trust, mismanagement and misappropriation of the waqf property but no decision was given by the Administrator of Waqf till 16-1-2016. It is also stated that Jamaluddin Khan died on 16-5-2016 and thereafter on 31-5-2016 the petitioner submitted his application to the Administrator of Waqf showing his appointment as Mutawalli of the said Waqf estate by registered deed dated 10-3-2004 and that neither the Administrator of Waqf nor the respondent No. 4 and other beneficiaries knew about the said deed dated 10-3-2004 earlier. It is further stated that the respondent No. 3 Deputy Administrator of Waqf after hearing all the parties by order dated 1-8-2016 rejected the application of the petitioner for appointment as Mutawalli and appointed the respondent No.4 as official Mutwalli in accordance with section 44 of the Waqf Ordinance, 1962 which does not call for any interference by this Court.

5. In an Affidavit-in-reply on behalf of the petitioner it has been stated that the application under section 32(1) of the waqf Ordinance, 1962 was filed by the respondent No. 4 in 2007 after 20 years of the said Jamaluddin Khan's appointment as Mutawalli with malafide intention and that the said respondent could not prove any of the allegations of mismanagement of the waqf estate. The proceedings against Jamaluddin Khan could not be completed by the respondent No.2 Administrator of Waqf due to the several applications for adjournments for long 9 (nine) years by the other respondents. Jamaluddin Khan by his letter dated 20-12-2015 informed the respondent No. 2 Administrator of Waqf about appointing the petitioner as Mutwalli after his death pursuant to the registered deed dated 10-3-2004. It is further alleged that the earlier Mutwalli Jamaluddin Khan complied strictly with the terms of Clause 1 of the Waqf deed and appointed the petitioner Mutawalli after his death. It is further stated that the respondent No.4 has not been able to prove or show that the said registered deed dated 10-3-2004 appointing him as Mutwalli or the aforesaid letter dated 20-12-2015 are forged or that the signature of Jamaluddin Khan on the said deed and letter is not his own and as such the impugned order appointing the respondent No.4 is illegal.

6. Mr Rafiq ul Huq assisted by Mr Ahmed Naquib Karim the learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that the petitioner was appointed Mutwalli by registered deed dated 10-3-2004 as per clause 1 of the Waqf Deeds dated 8-10-1945 and 13-6-1947 registration Nos. 857 and 2342 respectively and therefore the impugned order appointing the respondent No. 4 Mutwalli is illegal and not sustainable in law. The learned Advocate further submits that the impugned decision is ultra vires, arbitrary and illegal since it is in complete contravention of the Clause 1 of the said Waqf deed and section 43 of the Waqf Ordinance, 1962 and is liable to be set aside. The learned Advocate further submits that since the registered deed dated 10-3-2004 as well as late Jamaluddin Khan's letter dated 20-12-2015 appointing the petitioner Mutwalli before his death has not been claimed to be forged or illegal and therefore the appointment of the petitioner is in accordance with the wishes of the waqif and the original waqf deed and the same cannot be questioned and therefore the impugned order of the respondent No.3 Deputy Administrator of Waqf is not sustainable in law.

7. As against this, Mr Mahbubey Alam assisted by Mr M Fida Kamal and Md Raihanul Mustafa, the learned Advocates for the respondent No.4 submits that in the registered deed dated 10-3-2004 executed by late Jamaluddin Khan he has travelled beyond the wishes of the waqif and the original waqf deed. The learned Advocate submits that the respondent No.4 was appointed official Mutwalli by the respondent No. 2 Administrator of Waqf as the respondent No.4 was the elder brother of late Jamaluddin Khan who is a senior person of the family and competent to conduct the affairs of the waqf estate. Furthermore the learned Advocate further submits that in the said deed of 2004 late Jamaluddin Khan stated how future Mutwallis for the said waqf estate are to be appointed after the death of the petitioner which is contrary to the mode of appointment of Mutwalli stated by the waqif in the original waqf deed. Finally the learned Advocate submits that since the deed of 2004 was made malafide and contrary to the terms of the original waqf deed the said deed should be struck down in its entirety as has been done by the respondent No. 3 Deputy Administrator of Waqf . It has been further submitted that the petitioner was acting as Mutwalli prior to the death of Jamaluddin Khan since 2002 and he has been depriving the respondent No. 4 and other beneficiaries from the income of the waqf estate and therefore he has disqualified himself from being appointed as Mutwalli and the impugned order should not be interfered with.

8. It appears that the aforesaid waqf estate was created pursuant to waqf deeds dated 8-10-1945 and 13-6-1947 bearing registration Nos. 857 and 2342 respectively. After the death of the waqif Danu Mia became the Mutawalli. After his death Jamaluddin Khan became the Mutawalli. It may be mentioned that Jamaluddin Khan was alive during the life time of the waqif and he became Mutawalli in accordance with the terms and wishes of the waqf deed. It appears that by a registered deed dated 10-3-2004 Jamaluddin Khan appointed his son the petitioner as Mutawalli of the aforesaid Waqf estate upon his death Clause 1 of the Waqf deed states inter alia:

“যদি আমার ঔরষজাত কোন সন্তান সন্ততি জন্ম গ্রহণ না করে তাহা হইলে উক্ত মহাং দানু মিঞাই তাহার জীবদ্দশাকাল পর্যন্ত মোতওল্লী থাকিবে তাহার মৃত্যুর পর তাহার ঔরষজাত মহাং জামাল উদ্দিন খাঁন মোতওল্লী হইবে, সে তাহার জীবদ্দশাকাল পর্যন্ত মোতওল্লী পদে থাকিয়া আমার এই ওয়াকফ নামার নির্দেশ মত শাসন সংরক্ষণ ও পরিচালন করিয়া পরলোক গমন করতে পূর্বে তাহার নির্দেশানুসারে তাহার মোতওল্লী নিযুক্ত হইবে এবং থাকিবে, এই প্রকারে পুরুষানুক্রমে উল্লেখিতরুপে প্রত্যেক শেষোক্ত মোতওল্লীর নির্দেশ মতে মোতওল্লী নিযুক্ত হইয়া আমার এই ওয়াকফ সম্পত্বীয়াদী পরিচালিত হইতে থাকিবে”

The aforesaid provision clearly states that Jamaluddin Khan will have complete discretion to appoint a Mutawalli upon his death and the appointed Mutawalli will again be empowered to appoint his successor and in this way through the generations Mutawallis for administering the waqf estate will be appointed in accordance with the original waqf deed and wishes of the waqif. In the instant case the petitioner was appointed Mutwalli by the aforesaid registered deed dated 10-3-2004 by late Jamaluddin Khan. This matter of appointment was also communicated to the respondent No.2 by Jamaluddin Khan by his letter dated 20-12-2015 under the heading

মাননীয়,

ওয়াকফ প্রশাসক,

বাংলাদেশ ওয়াকফ প্রশাসকের কার্যালয়,

নিউ ইস্কাটন, ঢাকা।

সূত্রঃ ইসি নং- ১৩৫৯৮, হাজী আবদুল গনি ওয়াকফ এষ্টেট, চট্টগ্রাম।

বিষয়ঃ পরবর্তী মোতায়াল্লী নিয়োগ প্রসংঙ্গে।

জনাব, সূত্রে উল্লেখিত ওয়াকফ এষ্টেটের বর্তমান মোতোয়াল্লী হই। উক্ত ওয়াকফ এষ্টেটের পরবর্তী মোতোয়াল্লী কে হইবে তাহাকে নিয়োগ প্রদানের জন্য ওয়াকফ আমাকে নির্দেশ প্রদান করিয়াছেন। যাহা ওয়াকফ দলিলে স্পষ্টতঃ উল্লেখ আছে। তদানুযায়ী বিগত ১০-৩-২০০৪ ইং তারিখে আমি আমার একমাত্র পুত্র আবদুল্লাহ মোহাম্মদ এহতেশামকে পরবর্তী মোতোয়াল্লী পদে নিয়োগ প্রদান করিয়াছি। প্রয়োজনীয় অবগতির জন্য হুজুর সমীপে আমি অত্র নোটিশ প্রদান করিলাম।

অতএব, হুজুর সমীপে আমার বিনীত অনুরোধ আমার মৃত্যুর পর আবদুল্লাহ মোহাম্মদ এহতেশামকে সূত্রে উল্লেখিত ওয়াকফ এষ্টেটের পরবর্তী মোতোয়াল্লী হিসাবে নিয়োগ প্রদানে বাধিত করিবেন।

তারিখঃ ২০/১২/২০১৫ ইং

(মোহাম্মদ জামালউদ্দিন খাঁন)

মোতোয়াল্লী

পিতা-মরহুম হাজী দানু মিঞা

২৬৭, চন্দনপুরা, গণি বেকারী

থানা-চকবাজার, জিলা- চট্টগ্রাম,

হাজী আবদুল গণি ওয়াকফ এষ্টেট,

চট্টগ্রাম।

ইসি নং ১৩৫৯৮।

<u>9. From the aforesaid letter it is clearly apparent that the earlier Mutwalli Md Jamaluddin Khan appointed the petitioner Mutwalli of the aforesaid waqf estate and in the said letter the aforesaid registered deed dated 10-3-2004 has also been mentioned. There is nothing before us to show that the existence of the deed dated 10-3-2004 or the aforesaid letter dated 20-12-2015 has been disputed or that the same has been forged or obtained illegally. No evidence has been adduced or statement made that the signatures of late Md Jamaluddin Khan appearing on the aforesaid letter dated 20-12-2015 or registered deed dated 10-3-2004 are not that of Md Jamaluddin Khan. The only submission by the respondent No.4 is that since in his registered deed of 2004 Md Jamaluddin Khan has given directions for apportioning the income of the waqf estate and appointing subsequent Mutawallis from amongst his decedents contrary to the provisions of the original Waqf Deed therefore the entire deed appointing the petitioner as Mutwalli is to be disregarded. We find the said submission and reasoning totally misconceived; simply because certain provisions of the deed of 2004 are inconsistent with the original waqf deeds does not make the entire deed of 2004 invalid or illegal. The primary objective and purpose of the deed of 2004 was to appoint a Mutawalli for the waqf estate to administer it in accordance with the wishes of the waqif. The submission of the learned Advocate for the respondent No.4 that such appointment can only be made when the Mutwalli is on his death bed or when he is in fear of his death has got no substance whatsoever. Human life is uncertain and one never knows at what moment in time one will expire. It is sufficient if a Mutawalli makes an appointment of his successor in accordance with the terms of the original waqf deed and wishes of the waqif at any time before his death. In the instant case such appointment was categorically made in Md Jamaluddin Khan's deed of 2004 and subsequently communicated by him to the respondent No.2 by his letter dated 20-12-2015 under the heading “পরবর্তী মোতোয়াল্লী নিয়োগ প্রসংঙ্গে” leaving no doubt about late Md Jamaluddin Khan's appointment of the petitioner as Mutawalli.Although certain allegations have been made about the administration of the waqf estate by late Md Jamaluddin Khan during his life time, such allegations will not be any impediment to the appointment of the petitioner as Mutawalli of the said waqf estate. If the waqf estate is not managed and administered in accordance with the wishes of the waqif and the original waqf deeds under section 32(1) of the Waqf Ordinance, 1962 the beneficiaries can always lodge complaint to the Respondent No. 2 Administrator of Waqf. In such situation the respondent No. 2 is empowered to interfere. However, in the present facts before us section 44 of the Waqf Ordinance, 1962 empowering the Administrator of Waqf to appoint Official Mutwalli has no manner of application and therefore the impugned order of appointment of Mutawalli under the said provision of law appears to be illegal and is set aside.</u>

10. Accordingly, the Rule is made absolute. The impugned Memo No.16.02.0000.05.031. 396.57/273 (1-4) dated 1-8-2016 issued by the respondent No. 3 and notification published in the Daily Azadi on 4-8-2016, appointing respondent No. 4 Mutawalli is hereby declared to have been issued and published without lawful authority and of no legal effect.

There will be no order as to costs.

End.
